toolsets.name: AnimationAssistantToolset.SequencerDirectorToolset
toolsets.description:
Sequencer Director Blueprint toolset.

- GetOrCreateDirectorBlueprint(sequence) returns a UBlueprint handle that
  BlueprintToolset (AddFunctionGraph, AddFunctionParam, CreateNode,
  ConnectPins, CompileBlueprint, ...) and BlueprintDslToolset.Write operate
  on. Use it when the Director BP work needs low-level node authoring.

- AddEventKey(...) is a one-call wrapper that creates the endpoint on the
  Director BP, builds the FMovieSceneEvent, and adds the key on the event
  section's channel, for the simple "fire MyFunc on Player at frame N" case.

- CreateDynamicBindingResolver(...) creates a resolver function endpoint
  on the Director BP and binds it to the binding's FMovieSceneDynamicBinding.
  Returns the K2Node_FunctionEntry so callers can author the function body
  via BlueprintToolset.CreateNode / ConnectPins.

- CreateConditionEndpoint(...) does the same for a section or track condition.

tools.description:
Author a complete event key end-to-end on an Event track section.

Equivalent of the three-step manual flow:
  1. SequencerToolsFunctionLibrary::CreateQuickBinding to create an
     endpoint on the Director Blueprint that calls FunctionName on
     BoundObject (or its class).
  2. SequencerToolsFunctionLibrary::CreateEvent to wrap the endpoint
     in a FMovieSceneEvent bound to the event section.
  3. Find the event channel on the section and add a key at Frame
     carrying the FMovieSceneEvent value.
tools.name: AnimationAssistantToolset.SequencerDirectorToolset.AddEventKey

sequence.title: /Script/MovieScene.MovieSceneSequence

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

sequence.description: The LevelSequence that owns the event track + section.

eventSection.title: /Script/MovieSceneTracks.MovieSceneEventSectionBase

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

eventSection.description: The MovieSceneEventTriggerSection (or compatible) that the key lands on.

boundObject.title: /Script/CoreUObject.Object

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

boundObject.description: Object whose method or class member will be called by the event. Typically an actor instance resolved from a sequence binding.

functionName.description: Reflected UFUNCTION name on BoundObject's class (e.g. "SetActorScale3D"), NOT the spaced Blueprint-editor display name. CreateQuickBinding resolves it via UClass::FindFunctionByName, so a display name is rejected.

frame.description: Display-rate frame on the section where the event key is placed.

bCallInEditor.description: When true, the event will also fire during editor scrub (matches the CustomEvent's CallInEditor flag). Payload parameters: this entry point supplies no payload values, so any parameters the target function takes are left unset and default-construct when the event fires. That is fine for the common cases, but if you need explicit argument values, author the event through GetOrCreateDirectorBlueprint and BlueprintToolset instead. A warning naming the defaulted parameters is logged when the function takes any.

returnValue.description: True on success. False if any step failed; check the editor log for the specific failure (most often an unresolvable BoundObject/FunctionName pair).

tools.description:
Create a Director Blueprint Condition function endpoint on the sequence's
Director Blueprint and bind it to a director-blueprint condition on the
given host (a section, a whole track, or a single track row), so the host
only evaluates at runtime when the function returns true.

If the host has no condition, a Director Blueprint Condition is created on
it; if it already has one, that condition is reused. A host carrying a
different condition type (e.g. a platform or group condition) is rejected -
clear it first via MovieSceneConditionExtensions.ClearSectionCondition or
ClearTrackCondition.

Generates a function graph named after FunctionName whose entry node takes
an FMovieSceneConditionContext and returns a bool. The body is left empty by
design - author it via BlueprintToolset, then call
BlueprintToolset.CompileBlueprint on the Director BP so the condition's
CompiledFunctionName is populated; without that the condition is skipped at
runtime. The returned UK2Node_FunctionEntry is the new function's entry node.

Scope, CheckFrequency, bEditorForceTrue and payload variables are EditAnywhere
on the condition; set them via set_editor_property on the condition UObject,
obtained from the native accessor (e.g. section.get_section_condition()).
Retrieve the condition object before editing its properties; a class-path
string is not an object reference.

toolsets.name: AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset
toolsets.description:
Automation test discovery and execution toolset.

Wraps the IAutomationControllerManager API (the same backend the Session
Frontend uses) to let MCP clients list available tests, run them, and
retrieve results. Owns the automation controller lifecycle, handling session
discovery, worker communication, and test execution polling.

Typical workflow:
  1. DiscoverTests() once per session to initialize workers and load the test list.
  2. ListTests() to find tests by name or tag.
  3. RunTests() with the desired test names.
  4. GetTestStatus() / GetTestResults() to monitor and retrieve results.
  5. StopTests() to abort if needed.

tools.description:
Initialize automation worker discovery and load the test list.
Must be called once before ListTests or RunTests. Takes several seconds
as it discovers the local automation worker and enumerates all registered
tests. Returns an async result that completes with true when tests are
available, or an error if discovery fails.
tools.name: AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset.DiscoverTests

bForceRediscover.description: When true, bypass the cached report tree and re-poll workers. Used after reloading Python test modules mid-session.

Get a lightweight status snapshot of the automation controller.

Starts executing the specified tests and returns an async result that
completes with a summary when all tests finish.

returnValue.description: Value of the result.

tools.description:
Run automation tests selected by a filter expression. Requires DiscoverTests()
to have completed. Much faster than RunTests when targeting a large batch
because the engine narrows the report tree in a single pass instead of
running a per-leaf membership check against the requested name list.

Filter syntax (multiple expressions joined by '+'):
 "StartsWith:System.Engine"  prefix match against the full test path
 "^Foo"                       prefix anchor (equivalent to StartsWith:)
 "Bar$"                       suffix anchor
 "Substring"                  bare token matches anywhere in the path
 "Group:Smoke"                expand a named group from
                              AutomationControllerSettings ini Groups

Returns an async result that completes with the same summary shape as RunTests.

tools.description:
Applies ordered exact replacements to the latest session text. Revision must come from the
latest Read, Write, or Edit for the same asset and scope; otherwise call Read again.

The full batch is staged before mutation. The edit fails without a matching session, with a
stale Revision, when an OldString is absent or non-unique unless bReplaceAll is true, or when
the resulting DSL does not parse. Any failure leaves the asset unchanged.

When bDslOmitted is true, apply the replacements to your existing copy. Otherwise Dsl is the
authoritative canonical text for later edits.

assetPath.description: Content-browser path to the Blueprint.

oldString.description: Exact slice of the working DSL to replace. It must match verbatim and be unique unless bReplaceAll is true; include enough surrounding context to make it unambiguous.

bDslOmitted.description: True when Dsl is omitted: the canonical result is byte-identical to the text you could already predict, so your copy is correct as-is.

revision.description: New revision token. Use this to anchor subsequent Edit calls.

entry. Backtick-quote a segment containing spaces, syntax characters, or `/`; `` `A/B` `` is
one segment. Set bIncludePositions only when node positions are needed.

Returns one node type's schema as a DSL form. Query unfamiliar node types before writing:

  (node `Type`
    (in (`Pin` Type) ...)              ; data input pins
    (out (`Pin` Type) ...)             ; data output pins
    (params (`Prop` Type [:over]) ...) ; writable properties, baked as :`Prop` value
    (determines `Prop` ...))           ; properties whose value changes the pin set

(Enum A B ...) lists writable values. :over marks a property with an override input, supplied
as :`Prop` (wire Source). Write an (Instanced /Script/Pkg.Base) property with a concrete
class-headed value: (class:/Script/Pkg.Concrete :`Field` value ...). Empty sections are omitted.

Transactionally applies a DSL document and returns its canonical form and a new revision. A
failure leaves the asset unchanged.

Use Write for a complete document or a large structural change. Use Edit for a targeted
change that can be expressed as exact replacements against text you just read.

Top-level entries use upsert semantics: omitted entries remain and produce a warning. Delete an
entry with a tombstone such as (event `Foo` :!delete). Deleting a missing entry only warns.

Dsl is omitted when bDslOmitted is true because the submitted document is already canonical.

revision.description: New revision token. Use this to anchor subsequent Edit calls.

toolsets.name: ChaosClothAssetToolset.ChaosClothAssetToolset
toolsets.description:
Provides tools for creating and assigning ChaosClothAsset clothing data to skeletal meshes.
Replicates the workflow available via the SkeletalMesh Editor viewport context menu.

tools.description:
Binds a clothing asset to a specific LOD and section on the skeletal mesh.
Mirrors the SkeletalMesh Editor's "Apply Clothing Data" action.
Any clothing already bound to the section is unbound first.
tools.name: ChaosClothAssetToolset.ChaosClothAssetToolset.AssignClothingToSection

skeletalMeshPath.description: Object path to the target USkeletalMesh asset.

clothingAssetName.description: Name of the Clothing Asset on the mesh (e.g., from CreateClothingAsset or ListClothingAssets).

For ChaosClothAsset-derived types (bRequiresMatchingLodIndex == true in ListClothingAssets), pass the same value as LodIndex. For UClothingAssetCommon, pass the desired clothing LOD (0 to NumClothingLods-1 as reported by ListClothingAssets).

tools.description:

into a new UChaosClothAsset whose embedded Dataflow graph mirrors the legacy UChaosClothConfig and
UChaosClothSharedSimConfig values, with one WeightMap node per legacy weight map.
tools.name: ChaosClothAssetToolset.ChaosClothAssetToolset.ConvertClothingAssetCommonToChaosClothAsset

skeletalMeshPath.description: Object path to the USkeletalMesh that owns the legacy clothing asset.

clothingAssetName.description: Name of the UClothingAssetCommon on the mesh (from ListClothingAssets).

outputPackagePath.description: Folder where the new asset should be created (e.g. "/Game/Cloth/").

assetName.description: Name of the new asset; empty for default ("CA_Converted_<source>").

returnValue.description: Object path of the new UChaosClothAsset; empty on failure.

tools.description:
Creates a UChaosClothAssetSKMClothingAsset from a Chaos Cloth/Outfit Asset and adds it

tools.name: ChaosClothAssetToolset.ChaosClothAssetToolset.CreateClothingAsset

skeletalMeshPath.description: Object path to the target USkeletalMesh asset.

chaosClothAssetPath.description: Object path to the source UChaosClothAssetBase (cloth or outfit asset).

returnValue.description: List of created clothing assets, or empty if failed.

tools.description:
Returns the live solver counts for every clothing simulation running in PIE - the figures the
cloth debug UI shows, without opening it.

A simulation only reports counts once it is actually simulating.
tools.name: ChaosClothAssetToolset.ChaosClothAssetToolset.GetLiveClothSimulationStats

worldName.description: PIE world this simulation belongs to. In practice cloth only simulates on the client.

skeletalMeshName.description: Skeletal mesh asset driving this simulation, empty if none is set.

numDynamicParticles.description: Particles free to move. Zero on a simulation that exists but is not currently simulating.

numKinematicParticles.description: Particles pinned to the animated pose.

numIterations.description: Iterations in effect now. The solver adapts this to the frame delta, so it varies with framerate.

numSubsteps.description: Substeps in effect now. Framerate-dependent, as NumIterations above.

bCollidersSupported.description: Zeroes with this false mean the simulation does not report counts, not that it has none.

returnValue.description: One entry per simulation instance across all PIE worlds, empty outside PIE. Both client and server worlds are swept, so this is not one entry per character.

tools.description: Returns the name of clothing bound for a specific LOD section (if any).

assetName.description: Name of the clothing asset. Pass to AssignClothingToSection.

toolsets.name: CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset
toolsets.description:
AI debugger for CommonUI activation & focus routing in the current PIE session.
Snapshots the activatable tree and input-routing state per local player, diagnoses
why focus is (or isn't) where CommonUI intends it, logs activation/routing events
over time, and provides write tools to test hypotheses (activate/deactivate widgets,
refresh focus, lock the input type). Every tool other than the event-log tools raises
a script error when no PIE session is running.

tools.description: Activate a live activatable widget, as if the game had activated it.
tools.name: CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset.ActivateWidget

widgetName.description: Widget to activate: case-insensitive substring of the widget's object name or class name. Must resolve to exactly one live inactive widget in the PIE world; if several match, the error lists the candidates - pass a longer/exact name to disambiguate.

localPlayerIndex.description: Restrict matching to this player's widgets; -1 = any player.

tools.description:
Deactivate a live activatable widget. Same addressing rules as ActivateWidget,
but matches only currently-active widgets.
tools.name: CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset.DeactivateWidget

widgetName.description: Case-insensitive substring of object or class name; must be unambiguous.

localPlayerIndex.description: Restrict matching to this player's widgets; -1 = any player.

tools.description: All UI action bindings currently active (reachable by input) for a player.
tools.name: CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset.GetActionBindings

debugString.description: FUIActionBinding::ToDebugString() - includes key mappings and hold state.

returnValue.description: The active bindings across the matching players; empty when they hold none. Raises a script error when there is no PIE session, or when LocalPlayerIndex names a player with no CommonUI action router.

tools.description:
Snapshot of the CommonUI activatable tree: root nodes, action-domain roots with
children and bindings, active root, leafmost active widget, and optionally the
full-depth indented tree dump text.
tools.name: CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset.GetActivatableTree

bIncludeFullDump.description: Include the full-depth tree text (captured from the CommonUI.DumpActivatableTree console command); false = structured one-level data only.

leafmostClassName.description: Class name of the leafmost active widget within this root; empty if none or root not active.

paintLayer.description: Slate layer id of the widget's cached Slate widget; INDEX_NONE when it has none.

bIsInvalid.description: The node outlived the widget it represents; every field but NumActionBindings is empty.

numActionBindings.description: Bindings held by the node, including any whose handle no longer resolves; Bindings can be shorter.

ownerWidgetName.description: Name of the widget the binding was registered against; empty once that widget is gone.

treeNodes.description:
Every node of every root, full depth, pre-order. RootNodes and ActionDomainRoots describe only the
top of the tree; this is the whole of it, and the one source to build a tree view from.

domainName.description: Empty for a root outside every action domain.

bIsActiveRoot.description: The root the router currently routes input through. At most one root carries this.

treeRoots.description: The roots of TreeNodes, active root first and action-domain roots last.

fullTreeDump.description:
Full-depth indented tree text captured from CommonUI.DumpActivatableTree; empty when
bIncludeFullDump=false. For reading by a person: its shape is not a contract, so anything that
needs the tree should read TreeNodes and TreeRoots rather than parse this.

returnValue.description: One snapshot per matching player. Raises a script error when there is no PIE session, or when LocalPlayerIndex names a player with no CommonUI action router.

tools.description: The current status of the logger: on/off, event count, dropped count, time span, subscribed players.
tools.name: CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset.GetEventLoggingStatus

returnValue.title: CommonUIEventLoggerStatus
returnValue.description: Logging status.

subscribedPlayerCount.description: Routers currently subscribed (one per local player with a router).

tools.description:
Chronological digest of logged events, oldest first. Never carries callstacks; use
GetLoggedEvents when those are wanted.
tools.name: CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset.GetEventTimeline

maxCount.description: Maximum entries, taken from the most recent; 0 or less = unlimited.

eventTypeFilter.description: Same values as GetLoggedEvents. Empty = all; anything else raises a script error listing the accepted values.

pIEInstance.description: PIE instance owning the player, INDEX_NONE outside PIE.

payload.description: Event-specific detail: new input mode/type, input config string, displayed widget, etc.

leafmostWidgetClass.description: Leafmost activatable class at the time of the event (routing context).

returnValue.description: The matching entries, oldest first. Empty when nothing was logged or nothing matched.

tools.description:
Where Slate focus actually is for a player and where CommonUI intends it to be: the focused
Slate widget, its UMG and owning-activatable identity, the leafmost widget's desired focus
target, and whether focus sits inside the active root and the leafmost hierarchy.
tools.name: CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset.GetFocusState

returnValue.title: CommonUIFocusState
returnValue.description: That player's focus state. Raises a script error when there is no PIE session or the player has no CommonUI action router.

focusedWidgetDebugName.description:
Focused widget as the Widget Reflector names it ("WBP_Asset [WidgetName]"), empty when nothing
is focused.

Unlike FocusedUMGWidgetName this needs no owning activatable, so it still identifies focus that
has landed outside the CommonUI tree - which is where naming the widget matters most, since
nothing else in this struct can then place it.

focusedOwningActivatableName.description:
Object name of the activatable that owns focus, which is what the tree dump keys nodes by.

The class name alone cannot identify a node: a designer-renamed widget reports an object name
unrelated to its class ("MyLoadouts_Categories" for a WBP_LoadoutScrollingList_C), so anything
correlating focus against the tree needs this rather than guessing from the class.

focusedUMGWidgetName.description:
Variable name of the UMG widget backing the focused Slate widget, empty when there is none.

Only widgets built from a UWidget have one: focus can land on a bare Slate widget created in
C++, in which case FocusedSlateWidgetType is the only identification available.

focusedUMGWidgetClass.description: Class of the UMG widget named by FocusedUMGWidgetName, empty under the same conditions.

tools.description:
Everything governing whether input reaches game vs UI for a player: active input
mode and config (mouse capture/lock, move/look ignore), the viewport and player
controller flags that can block input regardless of CommonUI state, current input
device type, input type locks, held keys, leafmost widget, and current Slate focus.
tools.name: CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset.GetInputRoutingState

bInputConfigSet.description: False when the router has never applied an input config; the config fields below are then defaults.

bViewportIgnoringInput.description:
True when the viewport client drops all input before it reaches the player controller,
which no amount of CommonUI state can compensate for.

bPlayerControllerInputEnabled.description: APlayerController::InputEnabled(); false means the controller consumes nothing regardless of routing.

bPlayerControllerMoveInputIgnored.description:
The controller's actual accumulated ignore-move state. Diverges from bIgnoreMoveInput when
something other than the active input config (stasis, a gameplay system) also pushed an ignore.

bPlayerControllerLookInputIgnored.description: The controller's actual accumulated ignore-look state; see bPlayerControllerMoveInputIgnored.

inputTypeLocks.description: Active input type locks as "Reason=Type" strings (from UCommonInputSubsystem::GetCurrentInputLocks).

focusedWidgetDebugName.description:
Focused widget as the Widget Reflector names it ("WBP_Asset [WidgetName]"), empty when nothing
is focused. The Slate type alone rarely identifies anything: a screen full of SButtons all
report "SButton", so this is what a reader can actually search for in an asset.

returnValue.description: One state per matching player. Raises a script error when there is no PIE session, or when LocalPlayerIndex names a player with no CommonUI action router.

tools.description: Logged events, filtered.
tools.name: CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset.GetLoggedEvents

widgetNameFilter.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against widget name and class. Empty = all.

eventTypeFilter.description: One of Activated/Deactivated/WidgetRebuilt/InputModeChanged/ InputConfigChanged/InputMethodChanged/DisplayedWidgetChanged/TransitioningChanged/ FocusRedirected. Empty = all; anything else raises a script error listing the accepted values.

maxCount.description: Maximum events to return; 0 or less = unlimited.

bIncludeCallstacks.description: Symbolicate and include captured callstacks (slow; only for small result sets).

pIEInstance.description: PIE instance owning the player, INDEX_NONE outside PIE.

payload.description: Event-specific detail: new input mode/type, input config string, displayed widget, etc.

leafmostWidgetClass.description: Leafmost activatable class at the time of the event (routing context).

returnValue.description: The matching events, newest first. Empty when nothing was logged or nothing matched.

tools.description: Ask the router to re-apply focus to the active root's desired focus target.
tools.name: CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset.RefreshActiveRootFocus

localPlayerIndex.description: The player whose router should refresh focus; raises a script error when that player has no CommonUI action router.

tools.description: Remove an input type lock previously added with SetInputTypeLock.
tools.name: CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset.RemoveInputTypeLock

reason.description: The lock key used when the lock was added. Raises a script error when the player holds no lock under that reason.

localPlayerIndex.description: The player whose input subsystem holds the lock.

tools.description: Lock the effective input type for a player until the lock is removed.
tools.name: CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset.SetInputTypeLock

inputType.description: One of MouseAndKeyboard, Gamepad, Touch. A type the running platform does not support is rejected and raises a script error rather than silently not applying.

reason.description: Lock key; a later remove must use the same reason. Must not be empty.

localPlayerIndex.description: The player whose input subsystem is locked.

tools.description:
Toggle an in-viewport overlay that outlines activatable widgets, color-coded by
activation/focus state: green bold with a black halo = leafmost active node, green dashed =
activated in the active-root chain, yellow dashed = activated outside the active root, dim
grey = deactivated (only with bIncludeInactive), cyan = the leafmost widget's desired focus
target, orange = the widget actually holding Slate focus, white dashed = active root boundary.
Outlines are stacked by Slate paint layer, so the widget CommonUI treats as topmost is drawn
on top. Each activatable's label ends in [ActivationFocus] or [NoActivationFocus]; labels of
widgets that opt out of activation focus are drawn in magenta.
A legend with the active input mode and type is drawn top-left. The overlay is
hit-test-invisible, so it does not perturb the input being debugged; it is PIE-only and
auto-disables on PIE end. A multi-client session gets one overlay per client window, each
showing only the players that window owns.
tools.name: CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset.SetTreeVisualization

bEnabled.description: Turn the overlay on or off. Enabling raises a script error when there is no PIE session or the session has no game viewport; disabling never raises.

bIncludeInactive.description: Also outline deactivated activatable widgets (dim grey).

bShowLabels.description: Draw widget names and state labels next to each outline.

bLeafmostOnly.description: Hide every activatable outline except the leafmost active node. Focus outlines are still drawn. Overrides bIncludeInactive.

bShowLegend.description: Draw the colour key and per-player input mode lines in the top-left corner.

tools.description:
Begin logging CommonUI events (widget activation/deactivation/rebuild, input
mode/config changes, input method changes, container displayed-widget/transition
changes) into an in-memory ring buffer. Restarting clears the buffer.
tools.name: CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset.StartEventLogging

bCaptureCallstacks.description: Capture a C++ callstack on each Activated/Deactivated event; heavier.

bufferSize.description: Ring buffer capacity (oldest events drop when full). Must be at least 1; a smaller value raises a script error and leaves the event logger untouched.

tools.description: Stop logging; the buffer is retained for querying. Does nothing when not logging.
tools.name: CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset.StopEventLogging

toolsets.name: ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary
toolsets.description:
Helper functions to animate Control Rigs in level sequences from Python, Blueprints, and AI tools.

Invalid inputs, inaccessible or read-only assets, and failed operations raise a script error (a Python exception)
instead of returning a sentinel. A boolean that answers a question or reports whether anything changed (for example IsolateLinkedAnimTrack)
is a result, not an error. Most functions need the level sequence open in Sequencer, and some need Animation Mode active.
Frame parameters are display-rate frames unless TimeUnit is TickResolution.
Transform spaces: Local is the control's value (relative to its parent and offset), Global is Control Rig (component) space,
and World is world space.
The SetLocalControlRig* setters and SetControlRigWorldTransform(s) raise, without setting or keying anything, when the rig overrides
the value on evaluation (a control driven by rig logic, for example an FK control matched to IK). The check is one rig evaluation per
call. SetLocalControlRig* check in the rig's current pose, so only when the frame (the first frame for plural setters) is the current time;
SetControlRigWorldTransform(s) evaluate the sequence at the first frame first. Layered rigs, constrained controls and interactive drags are not checked.

tools.description:
Add an anim layer containing the controls and objects selected in Sequencer, adding the Base layer first if the sequence has no layers.
With nothing selected it adds an empty layer named "Empty Layer <N>".
tools.name: ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary.AddAnimLayerFromSelection

returnValue.description: The index of the created anim layer

tools.description:
Set up auto-bake recorders for the linked anim sequences on the given bindings.
Equivalent to the "Add AutoBake" context-menu entry in the Sequencer UI.
tools.name: ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary.AddAutoBake

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

inBindings.description: The bindings to configure for auto-baking

tools.description:
Same as AddAutoBake, but links pre-created anim sequences instead of prompting for new ones.
No asset creation or export options dialogs are shown. Everything is validated first: if anything is invalid an error is
raised and nothing is changed. That includes a binding that already has a linked anim sequence, a null, incompatible,
repeated or already linked anim sequence, or an anim sequence the editor's asset reference filter refuses to link (as in UEFN).
The anim sequences are only linked, not baked here: like AddAutoBake the level sequence is dirtied and the auto-bake runs when

returnValue.description: The current preferences

transformGizmoSize.description: Editor-wide transform gizmo size offset, from -10 to 150; it also affects level and Sequencer gizmos.

bHideControlShapes.description: Hide all control shapes and gizmos.

bOnlySelectRigControls.description: Restrict viewport selection to Control Rig controls.

bLocalTransformsInEachLocalSpace.description: Transform each selected control in its own local space rather than a shared one.

bShowAllProxyControls.description: Show every proxy control, not only the selected ones.

bShowControlsAsOverlay.description: Draw control shapes on top of the scene.

bDisplayAxesOnSelection.description: Draw axes on the selected elements.

axisScale.description: Length of the selection axes; 0 or more.

axisThickness.description: Thickness of the selection axes; 0 or more.

bCoordSystemPerWidgetMode.description: Restore each gizmo mode's coordinate space when switching modes in the viewport.

bMirrorControlsOnKeys.description: When keys are selected, mirroring controls mirrors those keys at their times, keying only their channels; otherwise only the current pose is mirrored.

bMirrorControlsAtCurrentTime.description: With bMirrorControlsOnKeys, write the mirrored keys from the current time, each offset from the earliest selected key.

bMirrorControlsCopyTangents.description: With bMirrorControlsOnKeys, copy the selected keys' tangents onto the mirrored keys.

bMirrorControlsFlipTangents.description: With bMirrorControlsCopyTangents, flip the tangents on the channels whose values are mirrored.

bShowConstraints.description: Draw constraints in the viewport, as Toggle Constraints Visualization does.

bShowInactiveConstraints.description: With bShowConstraints, also draw inactive constraints.

bAutoKeyOnRelease.description: Key controls when a viewport drag is released rather than while dragging.

tweenNoiseAmplitude.description: Largest value offset BlendToNoise applies, at full blend.

tweenNoiseFrequency.description: BlendToNoise noise input units per frame; lower is smoother across frames.

tweenWaveAmplitude.description: Largest value offset BlendToWave applies, at full blend.

tweenWavePeriodSeconds.description: Seconds per BlendToWave sine cycle; 0 or less leaves the keys unchanged.

tweenWavePhaseOffset.description: BlendToWave phase offset, in radians; the Tween Settings' Wave Frequency Offset.

tools.description:
Replace the Control Rig on the track with a new Control Rig. Note it will now be owned by the track.
When the track's sequence is focused in Sequencer, a rig with no bound object is bound to the track's skeletal mesh and initialized,
and the new rig replaces the old one in Sequencer and Animation Mode, so setting its values keys it. The new rig is constructed with the
track's settings and rotation order overrides, and the controls selected on the old rig are selected on it. One undoable step.
Raises a script error if the track is not a writable Control Rig track, the rig is already on it or on another track, one is layered
and the other is not, or the editor's asset reference filter refuses a reference from the track's sequence to the rig's asset (as in UEFN).
ReplaceControlRigFromReference creates the new rig from a Control Rig class or asset.
tools.name: ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary.ReplaceControlRig

tools.description:
Replace the Control Rig on a Control Rig track with a new rig created from a Control Rig class or asset, as
FindOrCreateControlRigTrackFromReference creates one. Keys on controls the new rig also has are kept, a layered track stays layered,
an FK rig keeps the old FK rig's apply mode, and the track is renamed after the new rig when it comes from a different class or asset.
The new rig is constructed with the track's settings and rotation order overrides, and the controls selected on the old rig are selected on it.
When the track's sequence is focused in Sequencer, the new rig is bound to the track's skeletal mesh and replaces the old one in
Sequencer and Animation Mode, so it can be read and keyed at once. One undoable step.
Raises a script error if the track is not a writable Control Rig track, the reference is not a Control Rig class or asset,
the track is layered and the new rig is not an FK rig and has no backwards solve event, or the editor's asset reference filter
refuses a reference from the track's sequence to the rig (as in UEFN).

tools.description:
Override a control setting on a Control Rig instance, as Anim Details' override view does: with an empty Value the setting's
current value is captured (Add Override), otherwise the setting takes Value (Edit Override Value). The override goes in the rig's
last linked override asset, creating one in the developer folder when it has none, and the rig is reconstructed so it applies.
PropertyPath is a control setting path such as TopologyControlSettings->DisplayName, TopologyControlSettings->bShapeVisible,
ShapeName, ShapeColor or ShapeTransform; Anim Details' names DisplayName, Shape->bVisible, Shape->Name, Shape->Color and
Shape->Transform are accepted too.
Raises a script error if overrides are disabled (ControlRig.Overrides), the Control Rig is null, the control does not exist,
the path is not a setting of the control, Value cannot be read as that setting, the override asset to edit is read-only, or an
override asset must be created and the rig has no asset or the developer folder is not visible or not writable in this editor
(as in UEFN).

toolsets.name: DataflowEditor.DataflowScriptingSubsystem
toolsets.description:
Builds, edits and inspects Dataflow graphs (UDataflow), standalone or embedded in an asset (e.g. a cloth asset).

A Dataflow asset contains a main graph, sub-graphs and variables. Graphs contain nodes linked through pins.
Graphs, nodes and pins are addressed by path:
- Graph: "" for the main graph, the sub-graph name otherwise
- Node:  "NodeName" in the main graph, "SubGraphName/NodeName" in a sub-graph; NodeName is the node's name, not its display name
- Pin:   "<NodePath>.PinName", e.g. "StaticMeshImport.Collection"

Node types are identifiers from ListNodeTypes: registered node types (e.g. "FAddFloatsDataflowNode"),
"SubGraph/<Name>" for a node running a sub-graph, and "Variable/<Name>" for a node reading a variable.
Data types are the Dataflow type names pins show, e.g. "float", "FVector", "TObjectPtr<UStaticMesh>", "TArray<int32>".
Values are in Unreal text export format, e.g. "1.5", "(X=1.0,Y=0.0,Z=0.0)" or "(1,2,3)" for an array.

Every change is one undo step. Errors raise, with a message starting with "[Code:Argument]". Assets are not saved.

Every function is both PythonCallable and an MCP tool (AICallable), registered with the toolset registry when it is loaded.

toolsets.name: editor_toolset.toolsets.python_scripting.PythonScriptingTools
toolsets.description:
Executes arbitrary, unsandboxed Python in the editor with full access to the
    `unreal` module, and looks up that module's API.

    Use this to call tools from a script with call_tool, chaining dependent calls and
    reducing large results before they return, and to reach the unreal API where no
    tool exposes the needed functionality or option, or when the user asks for a
    custom Python script.

tools.description:
Runs a Python script in the editor's interpreter on the game thread.

IMPORTANT: Call `read_me` once per conversation before using this tool,
for full usage instructions -- including how to compose other tools and
yield control during long-running work. Look up each `unreal` API with
search_symbols or get_symbol before calling it.
tools.name: editor_toolset.toolsets.python_scripting.PythonScriptingTools.execute_python

script.title: CodeBlock
script.description: Code block whose content is the Python source to execute. May contain top-level `await`.

content.description: The source text of the code block.

language.title: ECodeBlockLanguage
language.description: The language the content is written in. Value display names: Cpp = "C++".

returnValue.description: Value of the result.

tools.description:
Returns the documentation of a registered tool, or of a type, function, method, or property in the `unreal` Python API.

Pass a toolset or full tool name, a top-level name ('EditorActorSubsystem',
'log'), or a qualified 'Class.member'. A toolset returns its description
and the signature of each of its tools. A tool returns its signature,
description, and parameters. A function or member returns its signature and full
documentation. A type returns its description, then one line for each
editor property (inherited ones included), enum value, and method it
declares, and how many methods it inherits from each base; get_symbol on
'Type.member' or on a base gives the details. A struct only tools use
returns its fields and the tools that use it.
tools.name: editor_toolset.toolsets.python_scripting.PythonScriptingTools.get_symbol

name.description: Toolset or full tool name, top-level type or function name, a struct a tool signature names, or a qualified 'Class.member'.

returnValue.description: The documentation, or the assembled type API index.

tools.description:
Usage instructions for execute_python. Call this once per conversation
before using execute_python.

Explains the execution environment (namespace, async/await, composing
other tools) and, only when relevant, the spatial coordinate-conversion
helpers available in the current editor session.
tools.name: editor_toolset.toolsets.python_scripting.PythonScriptingTools.read_me

returnValue.description: Usage instructions as plain text.

tools.description:
Searches the registered tools and the `unreal` Python API for types, functions, methods, and properties.

Searches what this editor session provides, so every result exists here. Feed
a result's qualified_name to get_symbol to read it.
tools.name: editor_toolset.toolsets.python_scripting.PythonScriptingTools.search_symbols

pattern.description: Case-insensitive regular expression. Empty matches everything.

max_results.description: Maximum number of matches to return.

match.title: ApiSymbolMatch
match.description: What to match the pattern against: the symbol's own NAME, its SIGNATURE, or also its DOCUMENTATION (a type's includes its editor properties). A tool's signature includes its toolset; a member's does not include its class.

kinds.description: Only return symbols of these kinds. Empty returns all.

accepts.description: Only return functions, methods, and tools with a parameter of this type, and writable properties of it, alone or inside a container such as Array[...].

returns.description: Only return functions, methods, and tools that return this type, and properties of it, alone or inside a container.

returnValue.title: ApiSymbolSearch
returnValue.description: The best matches first, capped at max_results: a tool, type, or function named exactly the pattern; then other matches in a name, a tool's toolset included; then signature matches; then documentation matches. Within each, tools come first, then functions and methods, types, properties, enum and delegate types and members, and deprecated symbols; then whole words before parts of words. Ties go to the shorter name, then sort by name.

total_matches.description: How many symbols matched, including any beyond max_results.

obtained_with.description: For a subsystem type, the free function that returns its instance, or None when none is active. Empty for everything else.

qualified_name.description: 'Owner.member' for methods and properties; the bare name for types and free functions; the full tool name for a tool, which call_tool takes. Pass this to get_symbol.

symbols.description: The best matches, best first, at most max_results of them.

each of its gradients into one row of a lookup texture that materials sample with a Curve Atlas

Returns the property names on an object as dotted paths relative to Root, one element per property MaxDepth reaches,
parents before children, without types or descriptions (GetPropertySchema has those). A struct cut by MaxDepth ends
in " {...}". A container's bracket reports its live occupancy: "[0..2]" for array indices, ["Alpha", "Beta"] for map
keys, a bare count for a set (never indexable), "[]" when empty, and "[?]" below an unsubscripted container, where no
instance reaches. Narrow a range or key list to one entry before passing a path to GetProperties or SetProperties.

An object reference is a leaf: to list the object it points at, such as a component, pass that object as Instance.

root.description: Dotted path to list from. Empty lists the object itself. Subscript a container segment to list one element with its real occupancy; without a subscript it lists the element type, so everything below reports "[?]".

maxDepth.description: Levels below Root to expand. Zero or less expands every level. Defaults to one here so an agent cannot dump a whole object tree by accident.

toolsets.name: EditorToolset.UndoHistoryToolset
toolsets.description:
Tools for inspecting the Unreal Editor's undo history (the same queue shown in the Undo History
panel). Use these to see what recently changed and exactly which objects and properties each edit
touched, e.g. to ground "what did my last edits do?" questions.

tools.description: Returns transactions from the undo history, newest first.
tools.name: EditorToolset.UndoHistoryToolset.GetRecentTransactions

count.description: Maximum number of transactions to return; must be positive.

offset.description: Number of newest transactions to skip before collecting, for paging back through the history; must not be negative. 0 starts at the most recent.

label.description: Human-readable label for the transaction, as shown in the editor's Undo History panel.

returnValue.description: Up to Count transactions, newest first.

tools.description: Returns detailed information about a single transaction
tools.name: EditorToolset.UndoHistoryToolset.GetTransactionDetails

maxObjects.description: Maximum number of modified objects to include in ModifiedObjects, to keep the response compact for transactions that touch many objects (e.g. bulk deletes). Pass a larger value to see more, or 0 to fetch only the count.

returnValue.title: UndoHistoryTransactionDetails
returnValue.description: Details for that transaction.

label.description: Human-readable label for the transaction, as shown in the Undo History panel.

context.description: The system that created the transaction (e.g. the tool or editor), when recorded.

primaryObject.title: /Script/CoreUObject.Object

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

primaryObject.description:
The key object the transaction edited (e.g. the edited blueprint). Unset when the transaction
did not record a primary object.

bIsUndone.description: True when the transaction has already been undone and would be re-applied by the next redo.

totalModifiedObjects.description:
Total number of objects the transaction modified. May exceed the number of entries in
ModifiedObjects when that list was truncated.

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.
The reference stored as a soft path string.

changedProperties.description:
Names of the properties that changed on this object. May be empty when the change was
not a simple property edit (e.g. object created or deleted).

bHasNameChange.description: True if the object's name changed.

bHasOuterChange.description: True if the object's outer changed.

bHasExternalPackageChange.description: True if the object's assigned (external) package changed.

bHasPendingKillChange.description: True if the object's pending-kill state changed, i.e. it was created or destroyed.

bHasNonPropertyChanges.description: True if the object changed in ways beyond its properties (e.g. from custom serialization).

modifiedObjects.description:
The objects the transaction modified and which properties changed on each. May be truncated;
TotalModifiedObjects holds the full count.

tools.description:
Returns how far back a transaction is in the undo history, counted newest-first: 0 is the most
recent transaction, 1 the next, and so on.
tools.name: EditorToolset.UndoHistoryToolset.GetTransactionRecencyIndex

returnValue.description: The newest-first index, or INDEX_NONE (-1) when no transaction with that id is in the undo buffer.

tools.description:
Searches the undo history by transaction label using a fuzzy (edit-distance) match, closest
match first. When two transactions match a query equally well the more recent one is returned
first.
tools.name: EditorToolset.UndoHistoryToolset.SearchTransactions

query.description: Text to match against transaction labels. Case-insensitive. An empty query returns the most recent transactions.

count.description: Maximum number of matches to return; must be positive.

offset.description: Number of top-ranked matches to skip before collecting, for paging through results; must not be negative. 0 starts at the closest match.

label.description: Human-readable label for the transaction, as shown in the editor's Undo History panel.

editDistance.description:
Levenshtein edit distance between the query and the label, both lowercased. Lower is a closer
match; 0 means they are equal.

recencyIndex.description:
How far back the transaction is in the undo history, counted newest-first: 0 is the most
recent transaction, 1 the next, and so on.

returnValue.description: Up to Count matching transactions, closest match first, ties broken by recency.

toolsets.name: FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset
toolsets.description:
Reads and manages files and directories, edits text, and downloads HTTPS resources.
Relative native paths use the current working directory; absolute native paths are unrestricted.
Mounted Unreal paths use content directories. Unmounted plugin paths that the plugin manager finds use plugin directories. /Saved uses the project Saved directory.
Use file:// when an absolute native path overlaps an Unreal virtual path.

tools.description: Creates a directory and any missing parents. A directory that already exists is a success.
tools.name: FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset.CreateDirectory

path.description: Native, Unreal virtual-content, or plugin directory path.

returnValue.description: True when the directory exists afterwards.

tools.description:
Deletes one file.
Directories are rejected. Recursive deletion is unavailable. Source-controlled files are marked for deletion when source control is available.
tools.name: FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset.DeleteFile

path.description: Native, Unreal virtual-content, or plugin file path.

returnValue.description: True when the file was deleted.

tools.description:
Downloads an HTTPS URL to a file. Redirects are not followed. Responses above 1 GiB are rejected.
Local, private, and selected special-use addresses are rejected.
Only HTTP 200 responses succeed. Host resolution and the HTTP request each time out after 30 seconds.
Existing read-only files are checked out through source control before replacement.
tools.name: FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset.DownloadUrl

destinationPath.description: Native, Unreal virtual-content, or plugin destination path.

bOverwrite.description: Whether an existing file can be replaced.

returnValue.description: Always null

tools.description:
Edits the unique occurrence of a piece of text. Source files and results above 1 MiB are rejected.
Big-endian UTF-16 files are rejected. Existing read-only files are checked out through source control before replacement.
AnchorText is matched exactly first. If that fails, LF and CRLF variants are tried. NewText uses the file's existing line ending.
Replace changes the anchor text itself. InsertBefore and InsertAfter insert whole lines and preserve the anchor.
tools.name: FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset.EditTextByAnchor

path.description: Native, Unreal virtual-content, or plugin file path.

anchorText.description: Text locating the edit. It cannot be empty and must be unique.

newText.description: Replacement or inserted text. Empty text with Replace deletes the anchor.

editMode.title: EFileSystemEditMode
editMode.description: Whether to replace the anchor or insert around its line.

returnValue.description: The number of lines in the file afterwards.

tools.description:
Edits an inclusive range of one-based lines. Source files and results above 1 MiB are rejected.
Big-endian UTF-16 files are rejected. Existing read-only files are checked out through source control before replacement.
Lines outside the range remain unchanged, including their line endings. NewText uses the file's existing line ending.
tools.name: FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset.EditTextByLineRange

path.description: Native, Unreal virtual-content, or plugin file path.

firstLine.description: One-based first line in the selected range.

lastLine.description: One-based last line in the selected range, inclusive.

newText.description: Replacement lines. A trailing line ending is added when the file needs one.

editMode.title: EFileSystemEditMode
editMode.description: Whether to replace the range or insert around it.

returnValue.description: The number of lines in the file afterwards.

tools.description:
Lists a range from the immediate contents of a directory.
Directories with more than 100000 immediate entries are rejected before filtering or range selection.
tools.name: FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset.ListDirectory

path.description: Native, Unreal virtual-content, or plugin directory path.

firstEntry.description: One-based first entry to return after sorting by path.

maximumEntries.description: Result limit. bTruncated reports whether more entries remain.

returnValue.title: FileSystemDirectoryListResult

path.description: Path to the entry, in the same path form as the requested directory.

name.description: Entry name without its parent path.

bIsDirectory.description: True when the entry is a directory.

size.description: File size in bytes, or zero for a directory.

firstEntry.description: One-based first returned entry, or zero when Entries is empty.

lastEntry.description: One-based last returned entry, or zero when Entries is empty.

bTruncated.description: True when more entries remain after the returned range.

returnValue.description: Selected entries and their one-based range. Empty ranges use zero positions.

tools.description:
Reads lines or fragments without line numbers, budgeting the complete JSON response for EDA.
Decode Contents once as JSON when ContentsEncoding is "json-string" to recover NUL and U+FFFE/U+FFFF without transport substitution.
Oversized lines are returned in character-aligned fragments. Pass NextCursor to continue without losing text.
Supports UTF-8 and byte-order-marked UTF-16. Legacy single-byte text is not supported on all platforms.
tools.name: FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset.ReadTextFile

path.description: Native, Unreal virtual-content, or plugin file path.

firstLine.description: One-based first line to read. Ignored when ContinuationCursor is supplied.

maximumLines.description: Result limit. bTruncated reports whether more text remains.

continuationCursor.description: Cursor from the previous result, or empty for a new read. Detectable size/timestamp changes invalidate it; it is not a snapshot.

maximumResponseCharacters.description: Maximum Unicode characters in the compact JSON response, including returnValue and escaping. Defaults to EDA/TCS's 80000-character limit; use a smaller value if the deployment requires it.

returnValue.title: FileSystemTextReadResult

contents.description: Selected text, including original line endings. Decode according to ContentsEncoding before concatenating pages.

contentsEncoding.description: "text" is literal text. "json-string" is a JSON string literal: parse it once to recover text including NUL and U+FFFE/U+FFFF.

firstLine.description: One-based first returned line, or zero when no text is returned.

lastLine.description: One-based last returned line, or zero when no text is returned.

bTruncated.description: True when more text remains after the returned range.

nextCursor.description: Pass this opaque cursor to ReadTextFile to continue; empty when no text remains.

bStartsMidLine.description: True when Contents starts inside FirstLine rather than at its beginning.

bEndsMidLine.description: True when Contents ends inside LastLine. Continue with NextCursor, not LastLine + 1.

returnValue.description: Selected text and its one-based range. Empty ranges use zero positions.

tools.description: Resolves a native path, Unreal virtual-content path, or plugin path that the plugin manager finds to an absolute native path.
tools.name: FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset.ResolvePath

path.description: Native path, Unreal virtual-content path, or plugin path that the plugin manager finds.

returnValue.description: Absolute native path, or an empty string when the path cannot be resolved.

tools.description:
Writes a complete UTF-8 text file and creates missing parent directories.
Existing read-only files are checked out through source control before replacement.
tools.name: FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset.WriteTextFile

path.description: Native, Unreal virtual-content, or plugin file path.

bOverwrite.description: Whether an existing file can be replaced.

returnValue.description: True when the file was written.

toolsets.description:

load, activate, deactivate and unload, and editing their descriptor metadata.

tools.description:
Lists the additional metadata keys the GameFeatures subsystem is configured to read
from each .uplugin (UGameFeaturesSubsystemSettings::AdditionalPluginMetadataKeys),
sorted. These are the only keys SetGameFeaturePluginMetadataValue and
RemoveGameFeaturePluginMetadataValue will accept.

returnValue.description: Sorted list of configured additional metadata keys.

tools.description:
Reads the editable metadata on a Game Feature Plugin's .uplugin descriptor.
Returns the BuiltInInitialFeatureState and the configured additional metadata keys
(UGameFeaturesSubsystemSettings::AdditionalPluginMetadataKeys) with their values
rendered as JSON literals.
tools.name: GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset.GetGameFeaturePluginDetails

returnValue.title: GameFeaturePluginDetailsToolsetInfo
returnValue.description: Current details (BuiltInAutoState + AdditionalMetadata).

additionalMetadata.description:
Configured AdditionalPluginMetadataKeys mapped to their JSON-literal
values (e.g. "true", "\"v1.0\"", "{\"Major\":1}"). Keys come from
UGameFeaturesSubsystemSettings::AdditionalPluginMetadataKeys; values
the .uplugin does not specify round-trip as the empty string, matching
the engine parser's default.

pluginName.description: Name of the Game Feature Plugin.

returnValue.title: EPluginToolsetGFPState
returnValue.description: Simplified state enum. Raises an error if the subsystem is unavailable or the plugin is not found.

or the plugin is not found.
Use GetGameFeatureState if you need the current state when the plugin is not active.

pluginName.description: Name of the Game Feature Plugin.

returnValue.description: True if the Game Feature Plugin is active.

tools.description:
Return whether or not a plugin is a Game Feature Plugin. Will error if no plugin of this
name can be found by the Plugin Manager.
tools.name: GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset.IsGameFeaturePlugin

returnValue.description: True if the plugin is a Game Feature Plugin

tools.description:
Lists all discovered Game Feature Plugins sorted by name. This includes disabled plugins and
plugins the Game Features system has not registered, which the other tools cannot resolve.
Use the Plugins toolset to do general plugin enable/disable tasks.
tools.name: GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset.ListDiscoveredGameFeaturePlugins

returnValue.description: Sorted names of all discovered Game Feature Plugins.

Use the Plugins toolset to do general plugin enable/disable tasks.

returnValue.description: Sorted names of registered, enabled Game Feature Plugins.

tools.description:

After removal the key round-trips through AdditionalMetadata as an empty string --
that is the engine parser's default for missing keys, surfaced honestly.
tools.name: GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset.RemoveGameFeaturePluginMetadataValue

returnValue.title: GameFeaturePluginDetailsToolsetInfo
returnValue.description: Re-parsed plugin details reflecting the removal.

additionalMetadata.description:
Configured AdditionalPluginMetadataKeys mapped to their JSON-literal
values (e.g. "true", "\"v1.0\"", "{\"Major\":1}"). Keys come from
UGameFeaturesSubsystemSettings::AdditionalPluginMetadataKeys; values
the .uplugin does not specify round-trip as the empty string, matching
the engine parser's default.

returnValue.description: Value of the result.

tools.description: Requests deactivation of a Game Feature Plugin, which leaves it loaded.
tools.name: GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset.RequestDeactivateGameFeature

returnValue.description: Value of the result.

tools.description:
Requests load of a Game Feature Plugin without activating it. Use RequestActivateGameFeature

returnValue.description: Value of the result.

bKeepRegistered.description: Leave the plugin registered so its assets stay discoverable and it can be reloaded without rescanning. Pass false to also unregister it, which is what makes the editor stop reporting a plugin whose files are gone.

returnValue.description: Value of the result.

tools.description:
Sets the BuiltInInitialFeatureState on the GFP's .uplugin descriptor and writes the

returnValue.title: GameFeaturePluginDetailsToolsetInfo

additionalMetadata.description:
Configured AdditionalPluginMetadataKeys mapped to their JSON-literal

UGameFeaturesSubsystemSettings::AdditionalPluginMetadataKeys; values
the .uplugin does not specify round-trip as the empty string, matching
the engine parser's default.

Writes a value for one of the configured additional metadata keys to the GFP's

Configured AdditionalPluginMetadataKeys mapped to their JSON-literal

UGameFeaturesSubsystemSettings::AdditionalPluginMetadataKeys; values
the .uplugin does not specify round-trip as the empty string, matching

tools.description:
Creates an empty markdown base under the project's Content/KnowledgeBases folder, writes the marker
file that lets it be rediscovered on restart, and registers it. An empty base is valid; the first
WriteKnowledge creates its first file.
Raises an error if the alias is already registered or not a valid identifier, if RelativePath is not
one or two plain segments, if the directory already belongs to another base, or if it cannot be written.
tools.name: KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools.CreateMarkdownKnowledgeBase

alias.description: A short identifier for the base, e.g. "rigging". Lowercase, no spaces.

description.description: What belongs in this base and what question its entries answer, written for whoever reads ListKnowledgeBases next and has to choose between this base and the others.

relativePath.description: Where under Content/KnowledgeBases the base lives, e.g. "Rigging" or "Rigging/Conventions". No absolute paths, no "..".

returnValue.description: The alias of the created base.

tools.description:
Returns one entry by id with its full body. Ids are exact, so take them from QueryKnowledgeBase hits
rather than composing them; a miss names the nearest ids the base holds.
Raises an error if the alias is not registered or no entry has that id.
tools.name: KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools.GetKnowledgeEntry

entryId.description: The entry id, exactly as a hit reported it.

returnValue.title: KnowledgeBaseHit
returnValue.description: The entry, with bBodyTruncated false.

id.description: Pass to GetKnowledgeEntry for the full body, or to WriteKnowledge as EntryId to replace this entry.

body.description: The entry payload as JSON. Truncated unless this came from GetKnowledgeEntry.

bBodyTruncated.description: True if Body was shortened, so GetKnowledgeEntry will return more.

source.description: Where the entry came from. For a markdown base, the file path relative to the base, e.g. "limbs/ik-setup.md"; drop ".md" to reuse it as a WriteKnowledge FileId.

parent.description: The id of the prose entry explaining this one, or empty. Fetch it to learn why the entry exists.

score.description: Relevance, lower is better. Zero when the query carried no text.

tools.description:
Lists every registered knowledge base. Call this first: aliases are the handle every other tool takes
and they vary by project. Choose a base by its Description. A base with a "vocabulary" consumer is the
catalogue that tool's input is spelled from, so query it before calling that tool. Builds nothing.
tools.name: KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools.ListKnowledgeBases

alias.description: The handle every other tool takes.

description.description: What the base holds, what question it answers, and the tag vocabulary a query can filter on. Choose a base by this.

kind.description: "markdown" for a directory of files, "derived" for a base built from live engine state.

access.description: "reads", "writes", or "vocabulary". A vocabulary consumer spells its input from strings this base publishes, so query the base before calling it.

purpose.description: What the tool takes from the base, or puts into it.

consumers.description: The tools that use this base and how. Empty when the base is for you to read directly.

bWritable.description: True if WriteKnowledge can target this base. Derived bases are read-only.

returnValue.description: One summary per registered base, sorted by alias.

tools.description:
Lists the tags a base's entries carry, most common first, so a Tags filter is spelled from what exists
rather than guessed. Tags are exact strings: "simulation" does not match "Simulation".
Raises an error if the alias is not registered or the base fails to build.
tools.name: KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools.ListKnowledgeBaseTags

alias.description: The base to inspect, from ListKnowledgeBases.

prefix.description: Only tags starting with this, e.g. "layer:" for one family; empty for every tag.

limit.description: Maximum tags to return, or zero for all of them.

tag.description: The tag exactly as QueryKnowledgeBase's Tags filter needs it.

numEntries.description: How many entries carry the tag.

returnValue.description: Tags with the number of entries carrying each, most common first.

tools.description:
Searches one base. Text is matched as plain words and ranked; Tags keep only entries carrying all of
them; both empty lists the whole base. Bodies are truncated; GetKnowledgeEntry returns a hit's full payload.
Raises an error if the alias is not registered or the base fails to build.
tools.name: KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools.QueryKnowledgeBase

alias.description: The base to search, from ListKnowledgeBases.

text.description: Words to match, or empty to filter by tags alone.

tags.description: Tags an entry must all carry, spelled as ListKnowledgeBaseTags reports them; empty for no filter.

limit.description: Maximum results to return, or zero for all of them.

id.description: Pass to GetKnowledgeEntry for the full body, or to WriteKnowledge as EntryId to replace this entry.

body.description: The entry payload as JSON. Truncated unless this came from GetKnowledgeEntry.

bBodyTruncated.description: True if Body was shortened, so GetKnowledgeEntry will return more.

source.description: Where the entry came from. For a markdown base, the file path relative to the base, e.g. "limbs/ik-setup.md"; drop ".md" to reuse it as a WriteKnowledge FileId.

parent.description: The id of the prose entry explaining this one, or empty. Fetch it to learn why the entry exists.

score.description: Relevance, lower is better. Zero when the query carried no text.

returnValue.description: Hits, best first.

tools.description:
Writes a structured entry into a markdown base as a JSON block, preserving the prose and other blocks
in the file. An existing EntryId is replaced in the file that holds it, wherever that is; an empty
EntryId appends a new entry to the file FileId names, creating the file if absent. Reuse the stem of a
hit's Source as FileId so a topic accumulates rather than sprawls.
Only markdown bases are writable; check bWritable in ListKnowledgeBases first.
Raises an error if the alias is not registered, the base is read-only, BodyJson is not a JSON object,
or the file cannot be written.
tools.name: KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools.WriteKnowledge

alias.description: The markdown base to write into.

fileId.description: The file to add a new entry to, without extension, e.g. "ik-setup" or "limbs/ik-setup". Ignored when EntryId already exists.

tags.description: Tags to attach to the entry.

bodyJson.description: The entry payload as a JSON object. Stored verbatim when it carries no "_parent" member; one at the end is cut out, one anywhere else is removed by reserialising the object condensed.

entryId.description: Existing entry id to replace, or empty to append a new entry.

returnValue.description: The id of the written entry.

Every mutating tool takes a list, so a graph is described in one call rather than one per node

call rather than failing that one item.

toolsets.name: MVVMToolset.MVVMToolset
toolsets.description:
Toolset for authoring ModelViewViewModel (MVVM) data on UMG Widget Blueprints.

The Model-View-ViewModel pattern decouples a UMG widget's presentation (the View)
from the data and logic that drives it (the ViewModel). Bindings wire individual
widget properties to ViewModel properties so the UI reflects state changes
automatically, optionally routing values through conversion functions when the
source and destination types differ, and event bindings forward widget events
(multicast delegates) onto the ViewModel.

This toolset exposes an API to configure WidgetBlueprint's MVVM data:
  - Author ViewModel Blueprints derived from UMVVMViewModelBase and add
    typed properties to them.
  - Discover ViewModels on disk, attach them to a WidgetBlueprint, and list
    the ones currently registered on a widget.
  - Create, list, and remove property-to-property view bindings between
    widgets, ViewModels, and the WidgetBlueprint itself, optionally selecting
    a conversion function when types don't match.
  - Set literal values on a binding's conversion function arguments, or unbind
    an argument from its property path.
  - Create event bindings from widget multicast delegates to ViewModel
    handlers, enumerate the events available to bind, and set the literal
    values an event binding sends.
  - Create, list, and remove conditions that run a destination when a source
    value compares true against a constant, and change their comparison.
  - Repair MVVM state on a WidgetBlueprint by regenerating its binding graphs
    to match the stored binding data.

tools.description:
Adds a condition to the WidgetBlueprint's View: when the source value changes and compares true against Value (Value to
MaxValue for a Between operation), the destination is called or set. The widget blueprint is then compiled; compile
errors do not fail the call and are reported in the condition's CompileErrors. Not supported during PIE.

Values are compared as 32-bit floats. A destination function is called with default parameter values, and a destination
property is set to its type's default value, not to the source value.

tools.description:
Creates a View Binding from the SourceProperty to the Destination property.
If ConversionName is given, that conversion function is used, even if the property types already match (e.g. to format a FText).
Otherwise, if there is a type mismatch, an existing conversion function will try to be used.

Property paths resolve against each segment's declared type, so a field that only exists on a subclass of an intermediate
object's declared type won't resolve. Bind to the intermediate object and cast inside a conversion function instead.

Provides comprehensive access to Niagara System editing, including:
- System, emitter, and module creation and modification

toolsets.name: OptimusScripting.DeformerGraphScriptingSubsystem
toolsets.description:
Builds, edits, inspects and compiles Deformer Graph assets (UOptimusDeformer).

A deformer contains graphs (UpdateGraph always exists; SetupGraph and trigger graphs are optional),
variables, resources and component bindings. Graphs contain nodes linked through pins.

Graphs, nodes and pins are addressed by path:
- Graph: "UpdateGraph"
- Node:  "UpdateGraph/NodeName", where NodeName is the node's name, not its display name
- Pin:   "UpdateGraph/NodeName.PinName", sub-pins dot-separated, e.g. "UpdateGraph/MyKernel.Primary.Position"

Node types are "<Kind>/<Name>" identifiers from ListNodeTypes, e.g. "DataInterface/OptimusSkinnedMeshDataInterface".

Data domains: "" for a single value (parameter), "Vertex" for one value per vertex, "Vertex.Bone" for several
dimensions, "Vertex x 2" for a multiplier, "'Triangle * 3'" for an expression.

Every change is one undo step. Errors raise, with a message starting with "[Code:Argument]". Assets are not saved.

Every function is both PythonCallable and an MCP tool (AICallable), registered with the toolset registry when it is loaded.

toolsets.name: PerfToolset.CsvProfilerToolset
toolsets.description:
Reads CSV profiler captures (text .csv or compressed .csv.bin) named by a virtual content path, and
reduces them to bounded summaries: stat and event names, per-stat aggregates over a frame range, a
per-frame value window, and the event list. Raw capture bytes are never returned, so large captures
can be inspected without their contents entering model context.

tools.description:
Surveys a capture without returning per-frame values. StatGroups (the group histogram) is always
populated; individual stat names only when StatNameFilter is set.

GroupDepth groups the histogram by the first N segments of the '/'-delimited stat tree: depth 1
buckets under "Exclusive", depth 2 under "Exclusive/GameThread".
tools.name: PerfToolset.CsvProfilerToolset.GetCsvInfo

path.description: Virtual content path to a .csv or .csv.bin capture (e.g. '/Saved/Profiling/CSV/Foo.csv').

statNameFilter.description: Wildcard ('*'/'?'); matching stat names are returned. Empty returns no names; "*" returns all.

bIncludeAllMetadata.description: Return every metadata field instead of the curated subset.

groupDepth.description: Stat-tree levels to group by (>= 1); values below 1 are treated as 1.

returnValue.title: CsvProfilerInfoResult
returnValue.description: Survey of the capture.

frameCount.description: Number of frames (rows) in the capture.

statCount.description: Number of distinct stats (columns) in the capture.

statGroups.description:
Number of stats in each stat-name group, keyed by the group path at the requested GroupDepth
(e.g. "Exclusive" at depth 1, "Exclusive/GameThread" at depth 2); ungrouped stats bucket under
"(ungrouped)".

statNames.description: Stat names matching the requested filter.

eventNames.description: Distinct event names recorded in the capture.

metadata.description: Capture-level metadata (platform, build version, changelist, and similar).

tools.description:
Returns the capture's events with their frame indices. Repeats of the same event name on one
frame collapse into a single entry carrying a Count. FrameEnd -1 runs to the end; the defaults
return the whole run. At most Count events (the first in frame order) are returned.
tools.name: PerfToolset.CsvProfilerToolset.ListEvents

path.description: Virtual content path to a .csv or .csv.bin capture (e.g. '/Saved/Profiling/CSV/Foo.csv').

count.description: Maximum number of events to return.

frameEnd.description: Exclusive last frame, or -1 to run to the end.

returnValue.title: CsvProfilerEventList
returnValue.description: The event list.

name.description: Event name.

frame.description: Frame index the event was recorded at.

count.description:
Number of times this event name fired on this frame. Repeats of the same name within one frame
are collapsed into a single entry carrying this count.

events.description: Recorded events with their frame indices, capped at the returned count.

consideredCount.description: How many distinct event entries matched the range before the cap; exceeds Events.Num() when the result was truncated.

tools.description:
Returns up to Count per-frame values of one stat, starting at FrameStart. An over-large Count
clamps to the stat's own length rather than erroring; Count = -1 reads to the end of the column.
tools.name: PerfToolset.CsvProfilerToolset.ReadStatValues

path.description: Virtual content path to a .csv or .csv.bin capture (e.g. '/Saved/Profiling/CSV/Foo.csv').

frameStart.description: Inclusive first frame to read from.

count.description: Maximum frames to return from FrameStart; -1 reads to the end of the column.

returnValue.title: CsvProfilerStatValues
returnValue.description: The value window.

statName.description: The stat these values are for.

frameStart.description: Inclusive first frame of the returned window.

frameEnd.description: Exclusive last frame of the returned window.

tools.description:
Reduces each requested stat to average, min, max, total, and the P50/P90/P95/P99 percentiles over
a frame-index range. FrameEnd -1 runs to the end; the defaults reduce over the whole run. Stats not
present in the capture are omitted from the result.
tools.name: PerfToolset.CsvProfilerToolset.ReduceStat

path.description: Virtual content path to a .csv or .csv.bin capture (e.g. '/Saved/Profiling/CSV/Foo.csv').

frameEnd.description: Exclusive last frame, or -1 to run to the end.

returnValue.title: CsvProfilerReduceResult
returnValue.description: One reduction per stat found, keyed by stat name.

statName.description: The stat this reduction is for.

average.description: Mean of the per-frame values over the range.

min.description: Smallest per-frame value over the range.

max.description: Largest per-frame value over the range.

total.description: Sum of the per-frame values over the range.

stats.description: One reduction per stat that was present in the capture, keyed by stat name.

tools.description:
Ranks the capture's stats by a reduced aggregate (average, max, total, or a P50/P90/P95/P99
percentile) over a frame range and returns the top Count, each already reduced. A StatNameFilter
wildcard restricts the ranking to a group (e.g. "GPU*"); empty ranks all stats. FrameEnd -1 runs
to the end; the defaults rank the whole run.

Ranking is by raw aggregate value with no unit normalisation, so an unfiltered ranking mixes unit
domains (byte counters rank alongside millisecond timings).
tools.name: PerfToolset.CsvProfilerToolset.TopStats

path.description: Virtual content path to a .csv or .csv.bin capture (e.g. '/Saved/Profiling/CSV/Foo.csv').

toolsets.name: RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset
toolsets.description:
Rewind Debugger recording inspection toolset.

Exposes recorded session data — objects, events, property snapshots, and decoded trace events
from typed trace producers — to MCP clients, plus navigation entry points to drive the editor
UI to a specific recorded object and moment in time. Requires an active Rewind Debugger
analysis session (either a live PIE recording or a loaded trace file). Call GetSessionInfo
first to confirm a session is active before querying object data.

Typical workflow:
  1. GetSessionInfo() to confirm a session is active and get the time range.
  2. GetSelectedObject() to check whether the user already has an object focused in the
     outliner. If not, call ListObjects() to find objects by class name and get their ObjectIds.
  3. GetObjectEvents() / ListObjectTraceEvents() to see what events fired on an object
     in a time range. GetObjectEvents reads the generic gameplay-event channel;
     ListObjectTraceEvents aggregates typed trace producers that register an
     IRewindDebuggerToolsetEventDecoder (e.g. ChatCompletion).
  4. GetObjectProperties() to inspect property state at a specific moment, or
     GetTraceEventDetails() to decode a specific typed event in full.
  5. SelectObject() / SetScrubTime() to surface a particular object and moment
     in the Rewind Debugger UI when reporting findings back to the user.

Note: ObjectId parameters are typed `int64` because UFUNCTION reflection has no `uint64` binding,
but the underlying gameplay-provider object-id space is `uint64`. Values are bit-cast across the
boundary, so ids above 2^63 will round-trip as negative int64 through the MCP layer. In practice
engine-allocated ids stay well below that range.

tools.description:
Re-centres the Rewind Debugger visible view range on Time, preserving the current view width.
Independent of the scrub cursor: pair with SetScrubTime when you want to both move the cursor
and bring it into the centre of the visible timeline.

tools.description:

Returns {"Events": []} when no session is active or no events exist in the range.

Renders offscreen from the given world and camera using the specified mode.
Use ListModes for names available in this build and session; DescribeMode supplies interpretation
and sub-modes. Unknown or unavailable modes raise a script error. Mode names are case-sensitive.

tools.description:
Captures the current Game or PIE viewport as Slate draws it, with UMG and any other UI over the viewport, such as the recording border.
In PIE it redraws the window that holds the viewport; if that fails, the image shows the scene only, with a warning.
Metadata records the world and request time, not the originating GPU frame, camera, mode or internal resolution.
Output is an opaque 8-bit PNG, not a raw or HDR buffer export.
PQ/scRGB HDR uses the engine screenshot decoder and sRGB8 image conversion.
Conversion clips highlights and out-of-gamut channels without an additional tone curve.
A warning identifies this conversion.
Other HDR output encodings are rejected.

Raises a script error if the host cannot render, or if no initialized, readable Game/PIE framebuffer is available.
