toolsets.description:
Scripting for the Sequencer animation tools: motion trails, Time Posing and the Edit Pivot tool. Python: unreal.SequencerAnimToolsLibrary.
Every function raises a script error with the reason when it cannot do what was asked.
Functions that take a LevelSequence need it open and focused in the level editor's Sequencer.
Motion trail pin, space and offset functions need trails visible (SetMotionTrailsVisible); trail ids change whenever trails are
rebuilt (hidden and shown again, or a Sequencer opens or closes), so read them again with GetPinnedMotionTrails.
Frame parameters are display-rate frames unless TimeUnit is TickResolution.

tools.description:
Key actors transformed about a pivot at each frame, as the Edit Pivot tool does in Pose mode: the new world transform is
World * Pivot^-1 * Delta * Pivot. With bKeepOrientation the actors orbit the pivot and keep their rotation and scale, as Shift
does in the tool. Keys the actors in one undoable step. An actor that cannot be keyed (not bound in the sequence, or its

The stable identity. UMovieScene::AddMarkedFrame mints it for a new mark, UMovieScene::PostLoad stamps
one onto a mark saved before ids existed, UMovieScene::PostEditChangeProperty stamps a mark a reflection
write left without one and re-mints the copy a duplicate made, and UMovieScene::SetMarkedFrame keeps the
stored mark's.
Private so no hand-written code outside UMovieScene writes it: a copy of a mark this scene already
holds must not keep a shared identity, and AddMarkedFrame re-mints in that case. A mark arriving from
another scene keeps its id, because ids are unique within one scene only. Serialization, transactions
and CopyScriptStruct reach it through reflection regardless, which is what carries an id through a
save, an undo and the details panel's backing copy.
The friend declaration is wider than this member: it also opens Range and the private frame setters,
which must still only be written through SetRange and SetRangeStartAndEnd.

Editor-only because nothing outside the editor reads or maintains it: GetId, UMovieScene::FindMarkedFrameById
and all four write paths are editor-only too. Runtime names a mark by its label instead, which is what
FMovieSceneSequencePlaybackParams and FindMarkedFrameByLabel resolve against. PostLoad stamps a legacy
mark with an id derived from the scene's path, so a cook that keeps editor-only data is deterministic
even though the stamp never dirties the asset.

range.title: MovieSceneFrameRange
range.description:
Private so every write goes through SetRange/SetRangeStartAndEnd, which keep the stored range
canonical ([min, max) for a range, inclusive [S, S] for a single-frame mark, Start <= End) and
preserve the HasSerializedRange migration sentinel. Serialization and the details panel access
this through reflection regardless.

bIsDeterminismFence.description: When checked, treat this mark as a fence for evaluation purposes. Fences cannot be crossed in a single evaluation, and force the evaluation to be split into 2 separate parts. Only single-frame marks act as fences; this flag is ignored on mark ranges.

bIsInclusiveTime.description: Defines how this determinism fence determines the previous and next range: when true, the range will be dissected as (X, Y] -> (Y, Z], when false it will be (X, Y) -> [Y, Z].

(with the hit-test candidates considered) and the input that caused them, so an agent can
explain why a widget received focus. Registered focus-context providers (CommonUI, for one)
add framework state to each focus record. The same recording can be opened in the Navigation
Logger editor tab. Load this when investigating focus or gamepad/keyboard navigation in PIE
or in editor UI. Widget lifetime debugging (constructed, destructed, rebuilt) lives in
UMGDebuggerSubsystem.

toolsets.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset
toolsets.description:
Slate UI automation toolset.

Exposes snapshot, screenshot, and interaction tools for driving the
Unreal Editor UI programmatically.  Registered via UToolsetRegistry
so the ModelContextProtocol plugin picks them up automatically.

A shallow root observer (depth 0) continuously tracks top-level
windows.  Before working with a specific window or panel, call
Observe() on it to get deep widget coverage, then Unobserve() when
done.  Observers walk their subtree every ~100ms, assigning refs to
newly appeared widgets and keeping the ref cache current.

Input simulation uses direct Slate event APIs (ProcessKeyCharEvent,
ProcessMouseButtonDownEvent, etc.).

The one-shot action tools (Click, Hover, Scroll, Drag) leave no input held.
MouseDown, TouchStart and KeyDown do, so each needs its matching release;
ReleaseHeldInput drains whatever is left.

tools.description: Send an analog axis value along the target user's focus path; 1D axes only, send 0 afterwards to release.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.AnalogInput

key.description: FKey name of a 1D axis, e.g. "Gamepad_LeftX", "Gamepad_RightY", "Gamepad_LeftTriggerAxis".

value.description: Axis value, delivered unclamped; sticks -1..1, triggers 0..1 on hardware.

userIndex.description: Slate user to send to (default -1 = user mapped to the default controller); an explicit index must exist.

tools.description:
Click a Slate widget identified by its ref.
Returns false without clicking when the target point would not receive the event --
something is on top of it, the widget has no arranged size, or MouseDown still holds the
button. The log and LastRefusal() name the reason. True means the event was delivered to
the widget's branch, not that the widget handled it.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.Click

ref.description: Slate widget ref.

params.title: SlateInspectorToolsetClickParams
params.description: Button, double-click, modifiers and position; omitted fields keep their defaults.

modifiers.title: SlateInspectorToolsetModifierKeys
modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during the click.

position.title: SlateInspectorToolsetNormalizedPoint
position.description: Where in the widget to click.

tools.description:
Drag from one Slate widget to another (mouse down, stepped move, release).
Both ends are hit-tested first; returns false without dragging if either is covered
or unarranged.
The pointer is stepped along the path, so drag detection fires partway and the target
receives OnDragOver, including once at the drop point. Waypoints bend that path, for
gestures a straight line would not produce.
Start and end positions are normalized within each widget and default to the center. Use them to
aim at edge-band drop zones, e.g. EndPosition.Y = 0.1 to drop against the target's top edge.
Leave EndRef empty and pass MoveBy or Waypoints to drag StartRef by a distance instead of onto
another widget, e.g. splitters, sliders, scrollbars and divider grips. EndPosition is then
ignored, and a path that never leaves the press point is refused since the drag would not move.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.Drag

startRef.description: Slate widget ref for the drag source.

endRef.description: Slate widget ref for the drop target; empty means "drag StartRef itself".

params.title: SlateInspectorToolsetDragParams

Offsets from the press point visited in order before the drop, e.g. {"Points": [{"X": 60, "Y": 0}]}.
Use them for gestures a straight line would not produce, such as dragging around an obstacle.

x.description: Horizontal offset in screen pixels; positive is right.

y.description: Vertical offset in screen pixels; positive is down.

points.description: Offsets in visiting order, e.g. {"Points": [{"X": 60, "Y": 0}]}; empty means none.

endPosition.title: SlateInspectorToolsetNormalizedPoint
endPosition.description: Where in the target widget to drop, e.g. Y = 0.1 to drop against its top edge. Ignored when EndRef is empty.

moveByX.description: Extra screen pixels added to the drop point, positive = right.

moveByY.description: Extra screen pixels added to the drop point, positive = down.

Resolve a Slate widget ref back to the UMG UWidget that created it (for UMG
and PIE UIs). Returns the UWidget name, its UClass, the owning WidgetBlueprint
asset path, the enclosing UUserWidget chain, and a live Widget handle.
"resolvedVia" is "self" when the widget itself carries UMG metadata, or
"parent" when an ancestor did.
On failure Error is set and Widget is null: either the widget is pure Slate
with no UMG owner, or its authoring UWidget has since been destroyed. The
remaining metadata fields are still filled in for the latter case.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.GetUMGInfo

widget.title: /Script/CoreUObject.Object

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

widget.description:
The live UI-tech object wrapping the Slate widget (a UMG UWidget in practice).
Non-null exactly when Error is empty. Serialized as a {refPath} handle for use
with ObjectTools property accessors, which reflect over the instance's own class.

widgetName.description: UWidget name in its hierarchy, e.g. "SaveButton".

asset.description: Owning WidgetBlueprint asset path; empty when unknown.

tools.description:
Report whether a widget is reachable by pointer input, without changing anything.
Returns JSON {reached, samples, reachedSamples, x, y, reason}, using the same hit test Click,
Hover, Drag and Scroll refuse on; `reason` names the obstruction.
Grid > 1 samples a Grid x Grid lattice inset inside the widget instead of a single point.
`reachedSamples` counts the samples that hit, and x/y locate the first sample that missed.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.HitTest

ref.description: Slate widget ref.

params.title: SlateInspectorToolsetHitTestParams
params.description: Position and grid size; omitted fields keep their defaults.

position.title: SlateInspectorToolsetNormalizedPoint
position.description: Point to test when Grid is 1.

grid.description: Sample an N x N lattice inset in the widget instead of the single Position. Clamped to 1..16.

tools.description:
Hover over a Slate widget, triggering any hover state or tooltip.
Returns false without hovering when the target point is covered or the widget is unarranged.
Unlike the other action tools, Hover moves the OS cursor, since hover state only lasts while
the pointer stays over the widget. On Mac, Click, Drag and Scroll move it too and leave it
on the target, because Mac only routes pointer input to the window under the real cursor.
A button held by MouseDown stays held.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.Hover

ref.description: Slate widget ref.

params.title: SlateInspectorToolsetHoverParams
params.description: Position to hover; omitted fields keep their defaults.

position.title: SlateInspectorToolsetNormalizedPoint
position.description: Where in the widget to hover.

tools.description:
Press a key and leave it held; pair with KeyUp. Same key specs and gamepad routing as PressKey.
A held modifier key (LeftShift, RightControl, LeftAlt, LeftCommand, ...) is down for every later key event of the same
Slate user until released, by KeyUp or by a PressKey of the same key. It does not apply to pointer tools, which take
their own Modifiers, nor to the platform modifier state FSlateApplication::GetModifierKeys reports.
KeyUp or ReleaseHeldInput releases it, as does the hold watchdog after SlateInspectorToolset.HeldInputTimeoutSeconds without a pointer, touch, KeyDown or KeyUp call.
Returns true once the press is sent, whether or not a widget handled it, as a held modifier is normally unhandled.
False means nothing was sent because the key or user is invalid; LastRefusal() names the reason.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.KeyDown

key.description: Key spec with optional modifier prefixes, e.g. "LeftShift", "Ctrl+A", "Gamepad_LeftShoulder".

userIndex.description: Slate user to send to (default -1 = default controller or keyboard user); an explicit index must exist.

tools.description:
Release a key held by an earlier KeyDown for the same Slate user. Same key specs and gamepad routing as PressKey.
Returns true once the release is sent, whether or not a widget handled it, as most widgets act on the press.
False means nothing was sent because the key or user is invalid; LastRefusal() names the reason.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.KeyUp

key.description: Key spec with optional modifier prefixes, matching the KeyDown call.

userIndex.description: Slate user to send to (default -1 = default controller or keyboard user); an explicit index must exist.

tools.description:
Why the last action tool refused, as JSON {seq, tool, target, reason}; seq is 0 when nothing
has refused this session. seq increments on each refusal, so sample it before an action and
compare afterwards to tell a new refusal from one already read.
Click, Hover, Scroll, Drag, Type, Focus, SelectOption, PressKey, KeyDown and KeyUp record
refusals, and they record one every time they return false unless Slate is not running. For
PressKey that includes a key that was sent but that nothing handled. Read-only tools such as
Snapshot and HitTest never change it.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.LastRefusal

tools.description:
List all active observers as a JSON array for debugging.
Each entry includes the observer identifier, whether it is the root observer,
the root widget ref (if any), max depth, and cached snapshot size.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.ListObservers

tools.description:
Press a mouse button at a widget's center and leave it held; idempotent for a button this widget already holds.
MouseUp or ReleaseHeldInput releases it, as does the hold watchdog after SlateInspectorToolset.HeldInputTimeoutSeconds without a pointer, touch, KeyDown or KeyUp call.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.MouseDown

ref.description: Slate widget ref.

modifiers.title: SlateInspectorToolsetModifierKeys
modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during the press; none by default.

tools.description: Move the pointer to an absolute screen position; a button held by MouseDown stays held, so MouseDown/MouseMove/MouseUp drags.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.MouseMove

x.description: Horizontal screen position in pixels; positive is right.

y.description: Vertical screen position in pixels; positive is down.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during the move; none by default.

offsetY.description: Vertical offset from the widget center in screen pixels; positive moves down (default 0).

modifiers.title: SlateInspectorToolsetModifierKeys
modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during the move; none by default.

tools.description: Release a mouse button at the pointer, to its captor or whatever lies under it; safe without a prior MouseDown.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.MouseUp

modifiers.title: SlateInspectorToolsetModifierKeys
modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during the release; none by default.

tools.description:
Register an observer on a widget subtree so its refs are continuously
kept up to date (~100ms tick).  Call this on the window or panel you are
about to work with. It ensures new widgets appearing in that subtree
are assigned refs automatically.  Unobserve when you are done.
A shallow root observer (depth 0) already covers top-level windows.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.Observe

ref.description: Root widget ref to observe. Empty = all visible windows.

maxDepth.description: Maximum depth to walk from the root (default 30); negative values count as 0.

tools.description:
Press and release a key on the focused Slate widget; gamepad keys route as controller input for the target user.
Modifier keys held by KeyDown are down for the press, as with "Ctrl+" prefixes.
True means some handler consumed the press, an auto-repeat, its char event or the release, not that the UI
changed as intended. Any focusable widget handles Tab, arrow and D-pad keys as a navigation request, so true for
them does not mean focus moved; compare Snapshot or HitTest before and after. False means nothing handled the key,
or that nothing was sent because the key, user or RepeatCount is invalid; LastRefusal() names the reason, including
which widget had focus. In PIE, false can also mean the game viewport passed the key to the game and the game did
not consume it. Only BackSpace, Tab, Enter and Escape send a character; use Type to enter text.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.PressKey

key.description: FKey name with optional "Shift+", "Ctrl+", "Alt+", "Cmd+" prefixes, e.g. "Enter", "Ctrl+A", "Gamepad_DPad_Up".

userIndex.description: Slate user to send to (default -1 = default controller or keyboard user); an explicit index must exist.

repeatCount.description: Extra auto-repeat presses between the press and the release, 0..1000 (default 0).

tools.description:
Release every button MouseDown still holds, lift every finger TouchStart still holds and release every key KeyDown still holds, returning how many; buttons the user holds are left alone.
Also run by the hold watchdog after SlateInspectorToolset.HeldInputTimeoutSeconds (default 100) without a pointer, touch, KeyDown or KeyUp call, at PIE end and at shutdown.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.ReleaseHeldInput

tools.description:
Screenshot a Slate widget or an editor window. Prefer this over
SceneTools.take_screenshot for Editor UI; use SceneTools only for 3D viewport.
Pass a window ref from Windows("list") to capture a specific window; with no ref
it captures the active window, falling back to the main editor window when nothing
is active. A widget partly outside its window is cropped to the part inside it. Fails with an error naming the
reason when there is nothing to capture: an unknown ref, a widget in no visible window, or one entirely outside it.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.Screenshot

ref.description: Slate widget or window ref. Empty = active window, else main window.

mimeType.description: The format the image is encoded in.

data.description: The image data encoded as a base64 string.

cameraPosition.description:
World-space camera position at capture time.
Present in camera-rendered images (RenderLevelActors, RenderLevelPOVs).
cameraPosition.title: Vector

cameraRotation.description:
Camera rotation at capture time.
Present in camera-rendered images (RenderLevelActors, RenderLevelPOVs).
cameraRotation.title: Rotator

fOVDegrees.description:
Horizontal field of view in degrees at capture time.
Present for camera-captured images; absent for procedurally generated images
and asset thumbnails (which use ThumbnailTools::RenderThumbnail with no exposed FOV).

label.description:
Optional short identifier for the image. Producers that group images into
labelled sets (manifests, pair indices, named slots) can populate this so
downstream code or models can refer to a specific image by name.

tools.description:
Scroll the mouse wheel over a Slate widget.
Hit-tested like Click; returns false without scrolling if the point is covered or unarranged.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.Scroll

params.description: Ticks, gesture deltas, modifiers and position; omitted fields keep their defaults.

Wheel notches. Positive scrolls up / zooms in, negative down / out. The magnitude is clamped to 100.
0 sends no wheel event, and is refused unless a gesture delta is set.

Horizontal trackpad gesture delta in screen pixels, delivered as given; only widgets handling
OnTouchGesture react to it, since Slate's wheel carries no horizontal axis. 0 sends no gesture.

gestureY.description:
Vertical trackpad gesture delta in screen pixels, for widgets handling OnTouchGesture; prefer
Ticks for ordinary vertical scrolling. 0 sends no gesture.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during the scroll (Ctrl+wheel is zoom in many panels).

position.title: SlateInspectorToolsetNormalizedPoint
position.description: Where in the widget to scroll.

Select an option in a Slate combobox by its text label.
Opens the dropdown, finds the matching text, and clicks it.
tools.name: SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset.SelectOption

ref.description: Slate combobox ref.

tools.description:
Capture a Slate UI accessibility snapshot.  Use this to read the current
widget tree and discover refs for action tools (Click, Type, Hover, etc.).
A shallow root observer (depth 0) covers top-level windows automatically.
Before interacting with a specific window or panel, call Observe() on it
to get deep coverage, then Snapshot that subtree to see its contents.
Refs discovered by a previous Snapshot remain usable. You do NOT need to
call Snapshot again before every action.
Each [pos=X,Y size=W,H] is the widget's on-screen bounds in desktop pixels, whatever the DPI scale or rotation,
the same space as the pointer and touch tools' screen positions and offsets.

TouchEnd or ReleaseHeldInput lifts it, as does the hold watchdog after SlateInspectorToolset.HeldInputTimeoutSeconds without a pointer, touch, KeyDown or KeyUp call.

List, select, close or resize top-level Slate editor windows.
"list" returns a JSON array of {index, ref, title, active, regular, x, y, width, height}.

toolsets.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers
toolsets.description:
Editor source control common functionality.
Functions tagged AICallable are also exposed over MCP as the toolset "SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers".

@note Many of these source control methods use *smart* file strings which can be one of:
  - fully qualified path
  - relative path
  - long package name
  - asset path
  - export text path (often stored on clipboard)

  For example:
     - D:\Epic\Dev-Ent\Projects\Python3rdBP\Content\Mannequin\Animations\ThirdPersonIdle.uasset
     - Content\Mannequin\Animations\ThirdPersonIdle.uasset
     - /Game/Mannequin/Animations/ThirdPersonIdle
     - /Game/Mannequin/Animations/ThirdPersonIdle.ThirdPersonIdle
     - AnimSequence'/Game/Mannequin/Animations/ThirdPersonIdle.ThirdPersonIdle'

tools.description:
Adds files to source control; they are added on the next submit. Async: await the result.
The provider decides which files it accepts; a file it refuses, for example one that is already tracked, fails the call with its reason.

files.description: Files to add, as absolute or relative file paths, or content paths. Must not be empty.

returnValue.description: Always null

tools.description:
Checks files out, so they can be edited and submitted. Async: await the result.
The provider decides which files it accepts; a file it refuses, for example one that is not tracked or is checked out exclusively by another user, fails the call with its reason.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.CheckOut

files.description: Files to check out, as absolute or relative file paths, or content paths. Must not be empty.

returnValue.description: Always null

tools.description:
Creates a branch off the current branch. Async: await the result.
Does not change local files. Providers may refuse while there are pending changes, and may push the new branch to the server.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.CreateBranch

branchName.description: The name of the new branch. Must not be empty.

repository.description: The root directory of the repository to create the branch in. Empty uses the repository of the project.

description.description: Description for the changelist. Must not be empty.

returnValue.description: Value of the result.

tools.description:
Marks files for delete and removes them from disk, discarding any unsaved changes in their loaded packages.
Unloads the assets of the deleted files and reloads the open level when its map or external packages change,
so a deleted actor of a level that stores its actors in separate files disappears from that level.
Blocks until the delete and the reload complete. Game thread only.
Raises when no files are given.
Raises when source control is unavailable.
Raises when a file cannot be resolved.
Raises when the provider refuses a file, for example one that is not tracked; the error has its reason.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.Delete

files.description: Files to delete, as absolute or relative file paths, or content paths. Must not be empty.

returnValue.description: The absolute paths, with forward slashes, of the deleted files.

tools.description:
Deletes a branch for every user. Providers that keep history may archive it instead. Async: await the result.
Does not change local files. The provider decides which branches it accepts, for example it may refuse the current branch.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.DeleteBranch

branch.description: The name or id of the branch to delete. Must not be empty.

repository.description: The root directory of the repository the branch belongs to. Empty uses the repository of the project.

returnValue.description: Always null

tools.description:
Downloads a revision of a file to a local path, without changing the workspace. Async: await the result.
Refreshes the history of the file first.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.Download

file.description: The file, as an absolute or relative file path, or a content path. Must not be empty.

revision.description: The revision to download, for example a Revision value from the history. Empty downloads the latest revision.

destination.description: The file path to write the revision to; it must not exist yet, and its directory is created when missing. Empty writes to a temporary file.

returnValue.description: Value of the result.

tools.description:
Replaces the description of a pending changelist. Async: await the result.
The default changelist's description cannot be edited; to give its files a description, create
a changelist with CreateChangelist and move the files into it with MoveFilesToChangelist.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.EditChangelistDescription

changelistId.description: The identifier of a pending changelist.

description.description: The new description. Must not be empty.

returnValue.description: Always null

tools.description:
Returns the source-control state for an asset. Blocks until the provider answers. Does not write to the message log.
Raises when the asset does not exist or when the state cannot be read, for example when source control is disabled or unavailable.
A file that is not tracked by source control is not an error: bIsSourceControlled is false.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.GetAssetSourceControlState

assetPath.description: Content path of the asset.

returnValue.title: SourceControlAssetState
returnValue.description: The asset's source-control state.

bIsSourceControlled.description: Whether the asset is tracked by source control. False for local-only files (not yet submitted, or outside source-controlled directories).

bCanEdit.description: Whether the asset can be edited and saved. False only when another user holds an exclusive lock.

checkedOutBy.description: Name of the user holding the lock when bCanEdit is false. Empty otherwise.

tools.description:
Lists the files in a pending changelist, including files that are not content.
Raises when source control is unavailable or the changelist does not exist.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.GetChangelistFiles

changelistId.description: The identifier of a pending changelist.

filePath.description: Absolute local path of the file.

contentPath.description: Content path of the asset in the file. Empty for files that are not content, such as source or config.

action.description: What is pending for the file: "edit", "add", "delete" or "other".

returnValue.description: The files in the changelist. Empty for an empty changelist.

tools.description:
Returns the content paths of all assets you currently have open in source control
(checked out, marked for add, or marked for delete).

Non-content files (source, config, etc.) and anything that doesn't map to a mounted
content root are omitted. Files marked for delete are still listed.
Raises when source control is not enabled or the status refresh fails.

returnValue.description: Content paths of the opened assets. Empty when none are open.

Lists the pending changelists, including the default changelist.

numFiles.description: Number of files in the changelist.

returnValue.description: The pending changelists.

tools.description:
Lists submitted changelists, one page at a time, in the order the provider reports them, typically newest first. Async: await the result.
To get the next page, pass the last identifier of a page as Revision.

repository.description: The root directory of the repository. Empty uses the repository of the project.

returnValue.description: Value of the result.

tools.description:
Loads a historical revision of an asset alongside the currently loaded one. Async: await the result.
Treat the loaded package as read-only. It stays in memory until garbage collection runs.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.LoadAssetRevision

assetPath.description: Content path of the asset, such as "/Game/Foo/MyAsset".

revision.description: The value of the revision field of an entry returned by ListAssetRevisions. Empty loads the latest checked-in revision.

returnValue.description: Value of the result.

tools.description:
Merges the head of another branch into the current branch and reloads the loaded packages the merge changes,
including the open level when its map or external packages change. Blocks until the merge and the reload
complete. Game thread only.
Previews the merge first to find the affected files. Files changed on both branches may become conflicted:
resolve them before submitting. Providers may push the merge result to the server.
Raises when the branch is empty.
Raises when source control is unavailable.
Raises when the repository does not exist.
Raises, without merging, when a loaded package the merge changes has unsaved changes: save or revert it first.
Raises when the provider fails an operation; the error has its reason.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.MergeBranch

branch.description: The name or id of the branch to merge. Must not be empty.

repository.description: The root directory of the repository to merge into. Empty merges into the repository of the project.

returnValue.description: The absolute paths, with forward slashes, of the files the merge changed.

tools.description:
Gets the current source control states of files, refreshing them from the provider first. Async: await the result.
A file that is not tracked is not an error: its state reports bIsSourceControlled as false.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.QueryStates

files.description: Files to query, as absolute or relative file paths, or content paths. Must not be empty.

filename.description: Get the local filename that this state represents

bIsValid.description: Indicates whether this source control state has valid information (true) or not (false)

bIsUnknown.description: Determine if we know anything about the source control state of this file

bCanCheckIn.description: Determine if this file can be checked in.

bCanCheckOut.description: Determine if this file can be checked out

bIsCheckedOut.description: Determine if this file is checked out

bIsCurrent.description: Determine if this file is up-to-date with the version in source control

bIsSourceControlled.description: Determine if this file is under source control

bIsAdded.description:
Determine if this file is marked for add
@note        if already checked in then not considered mid add

bIsDeleted.description: Determine if this file is marked for delete

bIsIgnored.description: Determine if this file is ignored by source control

bCanEdit.description: Determine if source control allows this file to be edited

bCanDelete.description: Determine if source control allows this file to be deleted.

bIsModified.description: Determine if this file is modified compared to the version in source control.

bCanAdd.description:
Determine if this file can be added to source control (i.e. is part of the directory
structure currently under source control)

bIsConflicted.description: Determine if this file is in a conflicted state

bCanRevert.description: Determine if this file can be reverted, i.e. discard changes and the file will no longer be checked-out.

bIsCheckedOutOther.description: Determine if this file is checked out by someone else

checkedOutOther.description: Get name of other user who this file already checked out or "" if no other user has it checked out

bIsCheckedOutInOtherBranch.description: Determine if this file is checked out by someone else in another branch

bIsModifiedInOtherBranch.description: Determine if this file is modified by someone in another branch

previousUser.description: The username of the previous user to modify this file

returnValue.description: The states, one per file. Valid once the result completes without an error.

tools.description:
Marks conflicted mergeable files, such as text or Verse files, resolved once their conflict markers have been removed
from the files on disk. Edit and save the files first. Async: await the result.
Does not change the files. For files that are not mergeable, use ResolveMine or ResolveTheirs instead.
The provider decides which files it accepts; a file it refuses, for example one that still has conflict markers, fails the call with its reason.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.Resolve

files.description: Conflicted files, as absolute or relative file paths, or content paths. Must not be empty.

returnValue.description: Always null

tools.description:
Completes the resolution of conflicts, once every conflicted file has been resolved with Resolve, ResolveMine or ResolveTheirs. Async: await the result.
Providers may record the resolved files locally, for example by committing them to a personal branch.
The provider decides when it accepts this; for example it fails while conflicts remain or when the repository is not resolving conflicts.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.ResolveComplete

files.description: The files that were conflicted, as absolute or relative file paths, or content paths; they identify the repositories to complete. Must not be empty.

returnValue.description: Always null

tools.description:
Resolves conflicted files by keeping the local version, and reloads their loaded packages, including the open
level when its map or external packages change. Blocks until the resolve and the reload complete. Game thread only.
Raises when no files are given.
Raises when source control is unavailable.
Raises when a file cannot be resolved.
Raises, without resolving, when a loaded package of the files has unsaved changes: save or revert it first.
Raises when the provider refuses a file, for example one that is not conflicted; the error has its reason.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.ResolveMine

files.description: Conflicted files, as absolute or relative file paths, or content paths. Must not be empty.

returnValue.description: The absolute paths, with forward slashes, of the resolved files.

tools.description:
Resolves conflicted files by taking the incoming version, discarding their local changes, and reloads their
loaded packages, including the open level when its map or external packages change. Blocks until the resolve
and the reload complete. Game thread only.
Raises when no files are given.
Raises when source control is unavailable.
Raises when a file cannot be resolved.
Raises, without resolving, when a loaded package of the files has unsaved changes: save or revert it first.
Raises when the provider refuses a file, for example one that is not conflicted; the error has its reason.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.ResolveTheirs

files.description: Conflicted files, as absolute or relative file paths, or content paths. Must not be empty.

returnValue.description: The absolute paths, with forward slashes, of the resolved files.

tools.description:
Makes the synced revision the latest revision of the current branch again, by submitting a new revision with its content.
Blocks until the provider completes. Game thread only.
Raises when the description is empty.
Raises when source control is unavailable.
Raises when the repository does not exist.
Raises when the branch moved on since the last sync.
Raises when files the restore changes are checked out by other users; the error lists them.
Raises when the provider fails the operation; the error has its reason.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.RestoreAsLatest

description.description: The description of the new revision. Must not be empty.

repository.description: The root directory of the repository. Empty uses the repository of the project.

tools.description:
Restores a branch removed by DeleteBranch. Async: await the result.
Does not change local files. The provider decides which branches it can restore.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.RestoreBranch

branch.description: The name or id of the branch to restore. Must not be empty.

repository.description: The root directory of the repository the branch belongs to. Empty uses the repository of the project.

returnValue.description: Always null

tools.description:
Reverts files, discarding their local changes and any unsaved changes in their loaded packages, and reloads
those packages, including the open level when its map or external packages change. Blocks until the revert
and the reload complete. Game thread only.
Raises when no files are given.
Raises when source control is unavailable.
Raises when a file cannot be resolved.
Raises when the provider refuses a file, for example one that is not checked out; the error has its reason.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.Revert

files.description: Files to revert, as absolute or relative file paths, or content paths. Must not be empty.

returnValue.description: The absolute paths, with forward slashes, of the reverted files.

tools.description:
Releases the checkout of the given files that are checked out but not modified, so other users can check them out.
Refreshes the modified state of the files first. Does not change the files on disk, so their loaded packages are
not reloaded. Files that are not checked out or are modified are left alone. Blocks until the revert completes.
Game thread only.
Raises when no files are given.
Raises when source control is unavailable.
Raises when a file cannot be resolved.
Raises when the provider fails an operation; the error has its reason.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.RevertUnchanged

files.description: Files to consider, as absolute or relative file paths, or content paths. Must not be empty.

returnValue.description: The absolute paths, with forward slashes, of the files whose checkout was released. Empty when none was unchanged.

tools.description:
Submits a pending changelist after validating it, and fails with the validation errors if it
does not pass. Waits for the asset registry to finish scanning first. Invokes the Submit Tool
when one is available, as the Submit action in the Changelists window does; the user completes
the submit there, so the changelist is not yet submitted when the result completes.
Otherwise submits it directly. Async: await the result. Use this rather than submitting by
any other route.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.SubmitChangelist

changelistId.description: The identifier of a pending changelist.

returnValue.description: Value of the result.

tools.description:
Submits every pending change under the source control locations, without a changelist. Blocks until the submit completes. Game thread only.
Refreshes the status of the source control locations, then submits every file there that can be checked in.
Invokes the Submit Tool when one is available, as SubmitChangelist does; the user completes the submit there,
so the changes are not yet submitted when this returns. Otherwise checks the files in directly, after
virtualizing payloads when virtualization is enabled, which may append tags to the description.
Does not save, sync or validate first, and does not add files that are not tracked.
Raises when the description is empty.
Raises when source control is unavailable.
Raises when there is nothing to submit.
Raises when the Submit Tool fails to start.
Raises when the provider fails an operation; the error has its reason.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.SubmitChanges

description.description: The submit description. Must not be empty.

returnValue.description: A message that starts with "Submitted the changes" when they were submitted, or with "Invoked the Submit Tool" when the Submit Tool was started and the user must finish the submit there.

tools.description:
Switches to the head of another branch and reloads the loaded packages the switch changes, including the open
level when its map or external packages change. Blocks until the switch and the reload complete. Game thread only.
Previews the switch first to find the affected files.
Raises when the branch is empty.
Raises when source control is unavailable.
Raises when the repository does not exist.
Raises, without switching, when a loaded package the switch changes has unsaved changes: save or revert it first.
Raises when the provider fails an operation; the error has its reason.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.SwitchBranch

branch.description: The name or id of the branch to switch to. Must not be empty.

repository.description: The root directory of the repository to switch. Empty switches the repository of the project.

returnValue.description: The absolute paths, with forward slashes, of the files the switch changed.

tools.description:
Syncs to a revision and reloads the loaded packages the sync changes, including the open level when its
map or external packages change. Blocks until the sync and the reload complete. Game thread only.
Previews the sync first to find the affected files.
Raises when source control is unavailable.
Raises when the repository does not exist.
Raises, without syncing, when a loaded package the sync changes has unsaved changes: save or revert it first.
Raises when the provider fails an operation; the error has its reason.
tools.name: SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers.Sync

revision.description: The revision to sync to. Empty syncs to the latest revision.

repository.description: The root directory of the repository to sync. Empty syncs every repository of the workspace.

returnValue.description: The absolute paths, with forward slashes, of the files the sync changed.

Validates every pending change under the source control locations, without a changelist, the way the check-in dialog does.

verdict.description: Overall outcome across the changelist itself and every asset validated for it.

errors.description: Errors found in the changelist or any of its assets.

warnings.description: Warnings found in the changelist or any of its assets.

tools.description:
Renames a widget and updates the references to it. Returns updated widget info, or an empty info (with a script error) when the name is rejected.
References updated by the rename: widget animation bindings, property bindings, MVVM view bindings, Blueprint variable getters/setters, bound widget events
and other variable references in this blueprint's graphs and in loaded dependent blueprints, the desired focus widget, navigation rules and UI Component targets.
Not updated: references by name from C++ code, scripts or unloaded assets. Renaming a widget away from a parent class BindWidget property name drops that binding.
Rejected when the name is empty, too long, already used by another widget or object, or conflicts with an existing variable or function.
A name matching a parent class BindWidget property is accepted only if the widget is of that property's type, and then binds the widget to it.
Variables in child blueprints that collide with the new name are renamed. The blueprint is marked as structurally modified but is not compiled.

toolsets.description:
Places, edits and removes the 3D spatial annotations in the editor level, and controls how they display.

An annotation is either a placed proxy region (a shape that only draws into the annotation passes) or an
annotation on a scene actor, whose meshes are marked in the matte. Each carries a prompt and a colour group.
Creating and editing follow the "Persist New Annotations To Level" setting: scratch annotations never
dirty or reach the level.

Functions that take a group number accept 1-8 (1 red, 2 blue, 3 green, 4 orange, 5 pink, 6 purple, 7 cyan,
8 lime). The level editor must be up: an app without a level has nothing to annotate.

toolsets.name: UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationToolset
toolsets.description:
Exposes the 3D spatial annotation tools to the in-editor AI Assistant.

The assistant discovers tools through ToolsetRegistry, whereas these tools are registered
MCP-native (DECLARE_UNREALCANVAS_MCP_TOOL). The engine adapter only bridges ToolsetRegistry INTO
the MCP server and never the reverse, so without this class the annotation tools stay
invisible to the assistant even though they serve correctly on the MCP port.

Every function delegates to the matching MCP tool's Run(), so both surfaces share one
implementation of the actual work. Each wrapper validates its own arguments first; see its doc.

toolsets.description:
UMG Widget Animation toolset for AI-driven authoring of UWidgetAnimation assets.

UWidgetAnimation extends UMovieSceneSequence, so every UMovieSceneSequenceExtensions,
UMovieSceneTrackExtensions, UMovieSceneSectionExtensions, and UMovieSceneConditionExtensions
method that accepts a UMovieSceneSequence, UMovieSceneTrack, UMovieSceneSection, or
channel works on widget animations unmodified. Use this toolset for the UMG-specific

sections, keyframes, and conditions.

ObjectToBind must be either:
  - A UWidget inside the Widget Blueprint's tree (typical case: animate a child widget's properties).
  - A UPanelSlot whose Content is non-null (animate slot properties like padding/anchors).

The Widget Blueprint must have a compiled GeneratedClass. The implementation compiles the
blueprint if needed before binding.

toolsets.name: WidgetFinder.WidgetFinderSubsystem
toolsets.description:
Locates live Slate widgets with the Widget Finder query grammar, for agents, C++ and Python.
The service is off by default, so call StartService first. Until then nothing is mirrored and queries fail.
This toolset only finds widgets. Pass each result's `Ref` to the SlateInspectorToolset tools to act on it.
Prefer it over the SlateInspectorToolset Snapshot/Observe/Screenshot tools to locate widgets.

Owns the shared query service and the browser panel opened by `WidgetFinder.Open`.
Works in the editor, under -game and in cooked Development, Test and Shipping builds, but needs Slate.

tools.description:

Call this first when unsure of the syntax. The response's Description carries the signature-token legend.

description.description: What the term matches.

signature.description: Usage form. FWidgetFinderQuerySyntaxResponse::Description carries the token legend.

name.description: Parameter name (eg: value, x, step).

type.title: EWidgetFinderQueryParamType
type.description: What the parameter accepts, a literal or a nested node. See EWidgetFinderQueryParamType.

description.description: What the parameter means.

bOptional.description: The argument may be omitted, having a default.

bVariadic.description: Accepts one or more, comma-separated. Only ever the last parameter.

bAllowMatchAny.description: The `*` match-any token is allowed here. False forces a concrete value.

bAllowPartialMatch.description: A `*` inside the value is allowed (Sav*, *Button). False means exact tokens only. String parameters only.

rule.description: The constraint in words (eg: value should be 1 or more), which Signature states compactly.

members.description: Fields an aggregate ORs its value across. Empty for every other term.

tools.description:
Outline every match in the live UI with the Widget Reflector's debug border, to see what a query selects.
Needs a running service. Replaces any current highlight and persists until ClearHighlight or an empty query.
Detached matches count in TotalMatchCount but only draw once their tab or window is surfaced.

tools.description:
Locate live Slate widgets with a query, whose grammar GetQuerySyntax returns. Needs a running service.
Check bSuccess and ErrorMessage first, since a syntax error also returns no matches.
TotalMatchCount and bResultTruncated tell an under-constrained query from an exact one.
Pass each result's `Ref` to the SlateInspectorToolset tools to act on the widget.
Prefer Query and WaitForQuery over the SlateInspectorToolset Snapshot/Observe/Screenshot tools.

tools.description:
Wait, without polling, until a query's raw match count meets Comparison/Threshold, then return the matches.
Prefer it over repeated Query calls and over the SlateInspectorToolset Snapshot/Observe/Screenshot tools.
Completes once, with bConditionMet, or with bTimedOut after TimeoutSeconds, which still counts as success.
A bad query, a stopped service, or stopping the service mid-wait fails the call.

comparison.description:
Tested against the RAW live match count, never the Limit/Offset page.

threshold.description: The count the comparison tests against.

toolsets.name: WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset.WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset
toolsets.description:
AI assistant static-analysis tools over UMG widgets: widget tree descriptions, property override
tracing, and binding/event/delegate connection maps.
Load this when analyzing existing UMG / Widget Blueprint (UserWidget-based) UI assets.

tools.description:
Full structured description of every widget in the tree (or the subtree rooted at StartWidget).

Values are the designer-time state stored in the asset. Anything set at runtime (for example a
Blueprint graph changing a slot through SlotAsCanvasSlot, or style state that is not a
UPROPERTY) does not appear; use TraceWidgetPropertyOverrides for graph writes.

ComposedColors reports the composed pre-display **linear** tint only -- never a display-space
value, and never for URichTextBlock/CommonRichTextBlock (a fundamentally different
per-inline-tag-run model, excluded from v1 coverage). It does not model the contrast setting,
DisplayGamma, retainer boxes, Button's DisabledEffect, or widget animations.
tools.name: WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset.WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset.DescribeWidget

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

startWidget.title: /Script/UMG.Widget

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

startWidget.description: Root of the description; nullptr describes the whole tree.

maxDepth.description: 1 = no limit; 0 = StartWidget only; N = N levels.

propertyNameFilter.description: Substring match against property name; TEXT("") matches every property.

bSkipDefaultValues.description: When true (default), a property whose value matches the class default is excluded.

bIncludeFullDescription.description: When true, populates Description (verbose per-property text); defaults to false.

bIncludeComposedColors.description: When true, populates each entry's ComposedColors; defaults to false.

availableWidgetCount.description:
Widgets found within StartWidget/MaxDepth's bound. Keep alphabetically first: output keys are sorted,
and this is the canary if Widgets gets cut.

description.description:
Verbose per-property text tree; only populated when bIncludeFullDescription=true. Line [N] correlates 1:1 with Widgets[N]
(line breaks inside values are escaped as \n and \r, backslashes as \\).
Other value text is not escaped, so a value can imitate the line's own markers; read Widgets for
anything programmatic.

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

parent.title: /Script/UMG.PanelWidget

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

parent.description: Parent panel widget. nullptr when this is the root widget or lives in a named slot (see NamedSlotHost).

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

bIsVariable.description: Whether this widget is exposed as a blueprint variable.

depth.description: 0 at the walk's StartWidget; increases by one per level of descent (panel child or named slot content alike).

namedSlotHost.title: /Script/UMG.Widget

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

namedSlotHost.description:
Set when this widget is the content placed in a named slot on this host; nullptr otherwise.
Also nullptr for content in a slot inherited from a parent class (the widget tree hosts it); the
Description line still carries its "# named-slot" tag.

bInherited.description: True when this widget's name was already declared as a widget property on WidgetBlueprint's ParentClass.

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.
The reference stored as a soft path string.

uIComponents.description: UI components attached to this widget, in display order.

slotProperties.description: The widget's Slot object's reflected properties (padding, alignment, anchors, ...).

bResolved.description: True only when every factor resolved. When false, ComposedLinearColor is opaque black and means nothing.

composedLinearColor.title: LinearColor
composedLinearColor.description: Product of CompositionFactors, in evaluation order. Only meaningful when bResolved.

compositionFactors.description:
Ordered, e.g. ["Brush.TintColor", "AncestorColorAndOpacityTint", "BackgroundColor"]; always populated,
even when Gaps is not empty. AncestorColorAndOpacityTint includes the RenderOpacity of the widget and its ancestors.

gaps.description: One entry per factor that could not be resolved; empty when bResolved.

composedColors.description:
Composed rendered colour per interactable state; empty when no known formula for this widget kind,
or when DescribeWidget's bIncludeComposedColors is false.

widgets.description: Flat walk-order list, regardless of bIncludeFullDescription.

tools.description:
Reverse-searches every Widget Blueprint whose MVVM View references ViewModelClass, and returns
each one's own connection map grouped per widget. Each widget's rows are narrowed to just the
VMFieldBinding bindings to that exact ViewModelClass; call GetWidgetConnectionMap directly for
a widget's whole map. Native (non-Blueprint) ViewModel classes never surface here, since they
have no on-disk package identity for the reverse search to find.
tools.name: WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset.WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset.GetViewModelConnectionMap

viewModelClass.title: Class@/Script/ModelViewViewModel.MVVMViewModelBase

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

viewModelClass.description: The ViewModel class to search for.

scopeFilter.description: Same substring-match semantics as GetWidgetConnectionMap's ScopeFilter.

availableConnectionCount.description:
Sum of every referencing widget's own Connections.Num(). Keep alphabetically first: output keys
are sorted, and this is the canary if Widgets gets cut.

availableWidgetCount.description: Count of referencing Widget Blueprints found.

widgetPath.description: The widget's own soft object path, not a display name.

kindDetail.description: Only meaningful for EventBinding rows ("mvvm" vs "blueprint_bind"). Empty otherwise.

connectionName.description: The bound field/event/delegate's own name. For VMFieldBinding rows, the ViewModel's source field.

widget.description: The widget this connection is declared or found on.

targetVariable.description:
Set instead of Widget when a VMFieldBinding targets a class member variable rather than a
widget-tree property.

declaredIn.description: A graph name, "MVVM View", "Blueprint Bindings", or the scope searched if nothing was found.

widgets.description: Grouped per widget, not one flat list.

tools.description:
Maps every connection on WidgetBlueprint (MVVM field bindings, event bindings, delegates, and
legacy property bindings) into one pre-sorted checklist, Unconnected/Misconfigured rows first.
Misconfigured only applies to VMFieldBinding rows: Fixable if a conversion function can bridge
the types, Unbridgeable if none is allowlisted.
tools.name: WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset.WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset.GetWidgetConnectionMap

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

scopeFilter.description: Case-insensitive substring match against the row's Kind name (e.g. "VM", "Event", "Delegate", "Legacy"). Empty matches every kind.

availableConnectionCount.description:
Total rows matching ScopeFilter. Keep alphabetically first: output keys are sorted, and this is
the canary if Connections gets cut.

kindDetail.description: Only meaningful for EventBinding rows ("mvvm" vs "blueprint_bind"). Empty otherwise.

connectionName.description: The bound field/event/delegate's own name. For VMFieldBinding rows, the ViewModel's source field.

widget.description: The widget this connection is declared or found on.

targetVariable.description:
Set instead of Widget when a VMFieldBinding targets a class member variable rather than a
widget-tree property.

declaredIn.description: A graph name, "MVVM View", "Blueprint Bindings", or the scope searched if nothing was found.

tools.description: Returns the maximum depth of the widget tree. Depth: root with no children = 0; root + children = 1; etc.
tools.name: WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset.WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset.GetWidgetTreeDepth

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.
The reference stored as a soft path string.

returnValue.description: Depth as int32; -1 on error or when the tree has no root widget.

tools.description:
Traces every statically-discoverable write to a widget property across the whole tree, merging
Blueprint-graph writes with static origins (class defaults, archetype overrides, bindings).
Results are grouped per (widget, property) pair.

The highest-Order Applied entry is the Winner; earlier entries are Redundant, later ones Conflict.
With no Applied entry, the highest-Order entry is an uncertain best guess and all are Conflict.
tools.name: WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset.WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset.TraceWidgetPropertyOverrides

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

propertyNameFilter.description: Exact match against a property name. Empty traces every property with at least one write or archetype override.

widgetNameFilter.description: Exact match against a widget name. Empty traces every widget.

availablePropertyCount.description: Keep alphabetically first: output keys are sorted, and this is the canary if the arrays get cut.

order.description: Position within this entry's own (WidgetName, PropertyName) chain.

sourceDetail.description: Which widget variable this write targets, and whether it's a VariableSet or a setter call.

bCertain.description: True only when this winner's own ApplicationStatus is Applied.

winners.description: One row per distinct traced (widget, property) pair.

location.description: The write location this flag is about, matching the entry's own SourceDetail.
